Conflict of Interest Disclosure

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes the requirements for identifying, disclosing, managing, and resolving actual, potential, and perceived conflicts of interest for all Governing Body members, senior leadership, and key personnel of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Conflicts of interest — whether financial, professional, or organizational — pose a direct risk to the integrity of the Governing Body's fiduciary duty, the agency's regulatory compliance posture, and its standing with CMS and the OIG. This policy ensures that all individuals in positions of governance authority act solely in the best interest of the agency and the patients it serves, that no individual benefits personally from decisions made in their governance capacity, and that the agency maintains the transparent, documented conflict management program required by OIG Compliance Program Guidance for Home Health Agencies and expected by CMS surveyors conducting surveys under the State Operations Manual Appendix B.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

All voting and non-voting members of the Governing Body of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc.

The Agency Administrator

The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager

The Compliance Officer

Any contracted management entity or individual performing governing body functions on behalf of the agency

Senior leadership personnel who participate in budget approval, vendor selection, contract execution, or strategic decision-making on behalf of the agency

Any individual appointed to serve on a subcommittee of the Governing Body with decision-making authority

This policy does not apply to front-line clinical or administrative staff except to the extent they are appointed to a role listed above or are involved in a specific transaction or decision that gives rise to a conflict of interest subject to this policy.

4. Policy Statement

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. requires all individuals within the scope of this policy to place the interests of the agency and the patients it serves above any personal, financial, or organizational interest when exercising governance authority or making decisions on behalf of the agency.

4.2 All individuals within scope shall complete and submit a Conflict of Interest Disclosure Form (Appendix A) at the time of initial appointment, annually at the first quarterly Governing Body meeting of each calendar year, and within seven (7) calendar days of any change in circumstances that creates a new actual or potential conflict.

4.3 The Compliance Officer shall review all submitted disclosures, assess the nature and materiality of each disclosed conflict, and present a written summary of findings and management recommendations to the Governing Body within fourteen (14) calendar days of receipt.

4.4 Any individual with a disclosed conflict of interest shall recuse themselves from all discussion, deliberation, and voting on the matter to which the conflict pertains. Recusals shall be documented in Governing Body meeting minutes and in the individual's conflict of interest file.

4.5 The Governing Body shall formally act on all conflict of interest disclosures presenting a material risk to agency integrity, document its determinations in meeting minutes, and maintain a conflict management plan for each active disclosed conflict.

4.6 No Governing Body member, senior leader, or key personnel shall use their position of governance authority to obtain personal financial gain, preferential vendor treatment, employment benefits, or any other advantage for themselves or their immediate family members that is not available to the general workforce.

4.7 Failure to disclose a known conflict of interest, submission of a materially false disclosure, or failure to recuse from a matter involving a disclosed conflict shall constitute a violation of this policy and may result in removal from the Governing Body, termination of employment or contractual relationship, and referral to appropriate regulatory authorities.

4.8 All conflict of interest records — including disclosure forms, Compliance Officer reviews, Governing Body determinations, and recusal documentation — shall be maintained in a restricted access compliance file and retained for a minimum of seven (7) years from the date of disclosure in accordance with policy CO-HP-007.

4.9 This policy shall be reviewed annually by the Governing Body. Any revision requires re-acknowledgment by all individuals within scope within fourteen (14) calendar days of the revised effective date.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Initial Disclosure at Appointment

6.2 Annual Disclosure Process

6.3 Mid-Year Disclosure for Changed Circumstances

6.4 Materiality Assessment

6.5 Recusal Procedures

6.6 Conflict Management Plan Administration

6.7 Investigation of Undisclosed Conflicts

6.8 Escalation and Exception Handling

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance & Audit Considerations

8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For

CMS surveyors and OIG reviewers assessing the agency's compliance program under SOM Appendix B and OIG Compliance Program Guidance will specifically verify:

Evidence that a formal conflict of interest policy exists and is implemented. Surveyors will request the policy and verify it applies to all Governing Body members and senior leadership, not just the board chair.

Evidence of annual disclosure completion. Surveyors will request completed disclosure forms for all current Governing Body members and verify they are current. A disclosure form that is more than 12 months old without a renewal is a deficiency.

Evidence that disclosures are reviewed and acted upon. Surveyors will look for Compliance Officer review memos and Governing Body action in meeting minutes. A stack of disclosure forms with no evidence of review is a compliance program deficiency.

Evidence of recusal compliance. If surveyors identify a disclosed conflict, they will cross-reference meeting minutes to verify the individual did not participate in discussion or vote on the conflicted matter. Meeting minutes that do not document recusals are a common deficiency.

Evidence of conflict management plans for material conflicts. Surveyors will look for written plans defining how active conflicts are monitored. No plan means no management — surveyors treat this as a governance failure.

Evidence of a referral relationship review. OIG reviewers in particular will assess whether the agency has examined its Governing Body members' and senior leaders' relationships with referral sources and vendors for Anti-Kickback Statute risk.

Confidentiality and access controls on disclosure records. Surveyors will verify that disclosure forms are maintained in a restricted access file, not in general operational files visible to all staff.

8.3 Common Failure Points

9. References

9.1 Federal Regulations

9.2 CMS Guidance

9.3 OIG Guidance

9.4 Cross-Referenced Agency Policies

10. Training & Acknowledgment Requirements

10.1 All individuals within the scope of this policy shall receive orientation to this policy within fourteen (14) calendar days of appointment to a covered role. Orientation shall be conducted by the Compliance Officer and must cover: (a) the definition of a conflict of interest and examples relevant to a home health agency governance context; (b) disclosure obligations — when and how to disclose; (c) recusal requirements and procedures; (d) consequences of non-disclosure or failure to recuse; (e) available reporting channels for suspected conflicts by others; (f) whistleblower protections.

10.2 All individuals within scope shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix B) within fourteen (14) calendar days of the policy effective date, any revision, or new appointment.

10.3 Annual refresher on conflict of interest obligations shall be incorporated into the annual conflict of interest disclosure process at the Q1 meeting. The Compliance Officer shall distribute a written summary of key policy requirements and any updates with the annual disclosure forms. The Governing Body Chair shall confirm completion of the refresher in Q1 meeting minutes.

10.4 The Administrator shall maintain a tracking log of all policy acknowledgments and report any non-compliance to the Governing Body Chair within seven (7) calendar days of the acknowledgment deadline.

11. Version Control

11.1 This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per policy EN-LC-001.

11.2 Only the most current approved version of this policy, as reflected in the policy header, is valid for any operational, compliance, or regulatory purpose. All superseded versions must be archived and clearly marked as "SUPERSEDED — NOT FOR USE."

11.3 Any substantive revision to this policy requires: (a) review and approval by the Governing Body, documented in meeting minutes; (b) re-acknowledgment by all personnel within scope within fourteen (14) calendar days of the revised effective date; (c) update to the enterprise policy index per EN-TG-001.

11.4 Non-substantive revisions (formatting, typographical corrections, updated cross-references) may be approved by the Administrator with notification to the Governing Body at the next regular meeting.

Succession Planning for Key Leadership

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes the requirements for succession planning for the key leadership positions of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. — specifically the Administrator, the Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager, and the Compliance Officer. Leadership vacancies in these roles, if unfilled or inadequately managed, directly jeopardize the agency's regulatory compliance, patient safety, and operational continuity. CMS requires under 42 CFR § 484.105 that a qualified Administrator and Clinical Manager are in place at all times; extended vacancies without a designated interim constitute a Condition-level deficiency risk. This policy ensures the Governing Body maintains a proactive, documented succession strategy that enables the agency to fill or cover key leadership vacancies with qualified individuals without interruption to agency operations or compliance obligations.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

The Governing Body of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc.

The Governing Body Chair

The Agency Administrator

The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager

The Compliance Officer

The HR Director (in support of succession candidate identification and readiness assessment)

This policy governs succession planning for the following key leadership positions:

Administrator — the individual responsible for day-to-day management of the agency, appointed by the Governing Body per 42 CFR § 484.105(b).

Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager — the registered nurse responsible for oversight of all clinical services, per 42 CFR § 484.105(c).

Compliance Officer — the individual designated with authority and independence to operate the corporate compliance program per policy CO-CP-002.

This policy does not govern succession planning for positions below the three key leadership roles listed above unless specifically directed by the Governing Body.

4. Policy Statement

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a current, Governing Body-approved Succession Plan (Appendix A) identifying a designated interim successor for each of the three key leadership positions at all times.

4.2 The Succession Plan shall be reviewed and approved by the Governing Body at the second quarterly meeting (Q2) of each calendar year and updated within fourteen (14) calendar days of any key leadership vacancy, change in successor availability, or material change in the agency's organizational structure.

4.3 For each key leadership position, the Succession Plan shall identify: (a) the current role holder; (b) a primary interim designee who is pre-qualified and available to assume interim responsibility on short notice; (c) a secondary interim designee as backup; (d) the qualifications confirmed for each designee; and (e) the conditions and notification process for activating the succession plan.

4.4 Upon a key leadership vacancy — whether anticipated (planned departure, leave of absence) or unanticipated (sudden resignation, incapacitation, termination) — the Governing Body shall appoint a qualified interim designee within fourteen (14) calendar days of the vacancy and a permanent replacement within ninety (90) calendar days, consistent with the escalation requirements of policy GV-GB-001 §6.5.

4.5 An interim designee appointed under this policy must meet the minimum qualifications for the role as defined in policy GV-OG-002 (Administrator), applicable California state law (Clinical Manager), or policy CO-CP-002 (Compliance Officer). No individual shall serve as interim in a role for which they do not meet minimum qualifications.

4.6 The Succession Plan shall be maintained as a privileged, restricted-access document. Distribution shall be limited to the Governing Body, the Administrator, and the Compliance Officer.

4.7 This policy shall be reviewed biennially by the Governing Body, consistent with its ESSENTIAL classification tier. Any substantive revision requires re-acknowledgment by all individuals within scope within fourteen (14) calendar days of the revised effective date.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Development and Maintenance of the Succession Plan

6.2 Anticipated Vacancy Management

6.3 Unanticipated Vacancy Management

6.4 Permanent Replacement Process

6.5 Succession Plan Activation Log

6.6 Escalation and Exception Handling

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance & Audit Considerations

8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For

CMS surveyors conducting a standard survey under SOM Appendix B will specifically verify:

Evidence that the Administrator and Clinical Manager positions are continuously filled. Surveyors will confirm no undesignated vacancy exceeds 30 calendar days. They will request appointment documentation and verify interim designees meet minimum qualifications.

Evidence of a proactive succession plan. Surveyors increasingly look for evidence of governance planning rather than reactive crisis management. A documented, Governing Body-approved succession plan with named and pre-qualified designees demonstrates governance maturity.

Evidence that interim appointments were timely and documented. Surveyors will cross-reference the date of any vacancy against the date of interim appointment documentation. An undocumented gap is a survey risk even if the vacancy was brief.

Evidence that interim designees were qualified. Surveyors will request credential documentation for interim designees. An interim Clinical Manager who is not a currently licensed RN in California is a Condition-level deficiency.

Evidence that permanent replacements were recruited actively. Surveyors expect to see evidence of recruitment activity, not merely passive waiting, during the interim period.

8.3 Common Failure Points

9. References

9.1 Federal Regulations

9.2 CMS Guidance

9.3 Cross-Referenced Agency Policies

10. Training & Acknowledgment Requirements

10.1 The Administrator, Governing Body members, and each identified interim designee shall receive orientation to this policy within fourteen (14) calendar days of appointment or designation. Orientation shall cover: (a) the three key leadership positions covered; (b) qualification requirements for each role; (c) activation procedures for anticipated and unanticipated vacancies; (d) the 14-day interim and 90-day permanent appointment deadlines; (e) knowledge transfer expectations.

10.2 Each identified interim designee shall confirm in writing that they have reviewed this policy and understand their obligations upon plan activation. Written confirmation shall be maintained in the restricted governance file.

10.3 All individuals within scope shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix D) within fourteen (14) calendar days of the policy effective date, any revision, or new appointment.

10.4 The Succession Plan shall be reviewed biennially as a standing Q2 agenda item. The review shall include confirmation of designee willingness and qualification currency.

11.3 Any substantive revision requires: (a) Governing Body approval documented in meeting minutes; (b) re-acknowledgment by all personnel within scope within fourteen (14) calendar days; (c) update to the enterprise policy index per EN-TG-001.

11.4 Non-substantive revisions may be approved by the Administrator with notification to the Governing Body at the next regular meeting.

Annual Governance Self-Assessment

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes the requirements for the Governing Body of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. to conduct an annual self-assessment of its own governance effectiveness, regulatory compliance performance, and fulfillment of its oversight obligations. While not explicitly mandated as a standalone requirement by 42 CFR § 484.105, an annual governance self-assessment is the recognized industry best practice for demonstrating that the Governing Body is actively evaluating — and continuously improving — the quality and effectiveness of its governance functions. The self-assessment provides documented evidence that the Governing Body is not merely a passive recipient of reports but an active, reflective governance body that measures itself against defined standards. This evidence is increasingly relied upon by CMS surveyors assessing governance functioning under SOM Appendix B and by OIG reviewers evaluating compliance program effectiveness. This policy establishes a structured, consistent self-assessment process that produces a written record usable for continuous quality improvement, survey readiness, and strategic governance planning.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

All voting and non-voting members of the Governing Body of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc.

The Governing Body Chair (primary responsibility for process administration)

The Agency Administrator (support role — logistics, scheduling, record maintenance)

The Compliance Officer (support role — self-assessment tool preparation and results filing)

This policy governs the conduct of the annual Governing Body self-assessment only. It does not govern operational self-assessments, clinical audits, departmental performance reviews, or the QAPI program self-assessment activities, which are governed by their respective domain policies.

4. Policy Statement

4.1 The Governing Body of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall conduct an annual self-assessment of its governance effectiveness using the structured self-assessment tool provided in Appendix A of this policy.

4.2 The annual self-assessment shall be conducted at the first quarterly meeting (Q1) of each calendar year, immediately following or as part of the annual governance refresher training required by policy GV-GB-001 §10.4.

4.3 The self-assessment shall be completed individually by each Governing Body member and then reviewed collectively by the full Governing Body as a group discussion item. Individual responses shall remain confidential; only the aggregated findings and identified improvement priorities shall be documented in meeting minutes.

4.4 The Governing Body Chair shall prepare or oversee preparation of a written Governance Self-Assessment Summary Report (Appendix B) compiling the aggregated findings, identifying governance strengths, and defining a Governance Improvement Action Plan for any area rated as needing improvement.

4.5 The Governance Self-Assessment Summary Report and Improvement Action Plan shall be filed in the restricted governance file and referenced in Q1 meeting minutes as completed. Individual member assessment forms shall be maintained as privileged records accessible only to the Governing Body Chair and Compliance Officer.

4.6 At the Q1 meeting of the following year, the Governing Body shall review the prior year's Improvement Action Plan as the first step in the new self-assessment cycle, confirming which improvement actions were completed and identifying any that remain open.

4.7 This policy shall be reviewed annually. Any revision requires re-acknowledgment by all Governing Body members within fourteen (14) calendar days of the revised effective date.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Self-Assessment Preparation

6.2 Individual Self-Assessment Completion

6.3 Group Discussion and Findings Review

6.4 Governance Self-Assessment Summary Report and Improvement Action Plan

6.5 Improvement Action Plan Monitoring

6.6 Escalation and Exception Handling

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance & Audit Considerations

8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For

CMS surveyors assessing governance functioning under SOM Appendix B and OIG reviewers evaluating compliance program effectiveness will look for:

Evidence that the Governing Body is self-reflective and improvement-oriented. A documented self-assessment process with a written action plan demonstrates that the Governing Body takes its oversight responsibilities seriously and proactively identifies its own gaps — a hallmark of governance maturity.

Evidence that identified gaps are acted upon. Surveyors and auditors are skeptical of self-assessment processes that produce findings but no action. The Improvement Action Plan and quarterly monitoring evidence demonstrate follow-through.

Linkage between self-assessment findings and other compliance activities. Surveyors will look for evidence that critical gaps identified in the self-assessment triggered formal corrective action through the compliance program, not merely internal discussion.

Confidentiality and integrity of the process. While surveyors will not review individual member forms, they will assess whether the process appears genuine and structured versus perfunctory. A Summary Report that identifies only strengths with no improvement areas is likely to be viewed with skepticism.

8.3 Common Failure Points

9. References

9.1 Federal Regulations

9.2 OIG Guidance

9.3 Cross-Referenced Agency Policies

10. Training & Acknowledgment Requirements

10.1 All Governing Body members shall receive orientation to this policy within fourteen (14) calendar days of appointment. Orientation shall cover: (a) the purpose and value of the self-assessment as a governance improvement tool; (b) how to complete the Self-Assessment Tool (Appendix A) honestly and independently; (c) the confidentiality of individual responses; (d) how aggregated findings are used in the group discussion; (e) the member's responsibility to contribute meaningfully to the group discussion and action planning.

10.2 All Governing Body members shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix C) within fourteen (14) calendar days of the policy effective date, any revision, or new appointment.

10.3 The annual self-assessment process shall be conducted as part of the Q1 annual governance refresher per policy GV-GB-001 §10.4, integrating it into the established annual governance education calendar.

11. Version Control

11.1 This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per policy EN-LC-001.

11.2 Only the most current approved version of this policy is valid. All superseded versions must be archived and clearly marked as "SUPERSEDED — NOT FOR USE."

11.3 Any substantive revision requires: (a) Governing Body approval documented in meeting minutes; (b) re-acknowledgment by all personnel within scope within fourteen (14) calendar days; (c) update to the enterprise policy index per EN-TG-001.

11.4 Non-substantive revisions may be approved by the Administrator with notification to the Governing Body at the next regular meeting.

Organizational Structure & Reporting

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes the formal organizational structure, reporting relationships, and lines of authority for Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. A clearly defined organizational structure is essential to ensure that all personnel understand their reporting relationships, that accountability is maintained at every level, and that the agency operates in compliance with the organizational and administrative requirements of 42 CFR § 484.105. The Governing Body, as the ultimate authority for the agency's operation and management, must ensure that an organizational structure exists that supports effective service delivery, regulatory compliance, and clear communication from the Governing Body through all operational levels to the point of patient care.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

The Governing Body of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc.

The Agency Administrator

The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager

The Compliance Officer

All department heads, supervisors, and managers

All clinical and non-clinical employees, contractors, and per diem staff

All individuals performing services under the direction of the agency

This policy does not apply to patients, families, or external referral sources, except to the extent that organizational structure information is shared with these parties per patient rights requirements (CL-PR-001) or interagency agreement obligations (GV-EA-001).

4. Policy Statement

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a formally documented organizational structure that defines the reporting relationships, lines of authority, and accountability for all agency functions, as required by 42 CFR § 484.105(a) and California Health and Safety Code requirements for home health agencies.

4.2 The organizational structure shall clearly delineate the relationship between the Governing Body, the Administrator, the Clinical Manager (Director of Nursing), the Compliance Officer, and all departments and positions within the agency.

4.3 The Administrator shall maintain a current organizational chart that accurately reflects the agency's structure. The organizational chart shall be approved by the Governing Body and updated within 14 calendar days of any change to leadership positions, departmental structure, or reporting relationships.

4.4 The organizational structure shall ensure that:

The Administrator reports directly to the Governing Body (GV-GB-001, GV-OG-002)

The Clinical Manager / Director of Nursing has direct authority over all clinical operations (GV-OG-002, 42 CFR § 484.105(c))

The Compliance Officer has a direct reporting line to the Governing Body independent of the Administrator for compliance matters (CO-CP-002)

All clinical staff have a defined clinical supervision chain that terminates at the Director of Nursing

All administrative and operational staff have a defined management chain that terminates at the Administrator

4.5 No individual shall be required to report to two supervisors for the same function without a formally documented dual-reporting arrangement approved by the Administrator and documented in the individual's job description (HR-JD domain).

4.6 The organizational structure shall support the agency's defined scope of services (GV-OG-003) and shall be staffed at levels sufficient to deliver all authorized services safely and effectively (HR-WM-001).

4.7 When the agency operates branch offices or satellite locations, the organizational structure must clearly identify the supervisory relationships and reporting lines for those locations back to the central office, per policy OP-FM-002.

4.8 Only the most current approved version of this policy and the associated organizational chart shall be considered valid. Superseded versions must not be used for any operational or compliance purpose. Any revision to this policy requires re-acknowledgment by all personnel within scope within 14 calendar days of the revised effective date.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Establishment and Documentation of the Organizational Structure

6.2 Required Organizational Positions and Reporting Lines

The following positions and reporting lines are required to meet 42 CFR § 484.105 and California state requirements. The Governing Body shall ensure these positions are filled at all times (per GV-GB-001, Section 6.2.2 and Section 6.5).

6.3 Annual Review and Update of the Organizational Structure

6.4 Changes to the Organizational Structure

6.5 Communication of the Organizational Structure

6.6 Escalation and Exception Handling

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance & Audit Considerations

8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For

CMS surveyors conducting a standard survey under the State Operations Manual (SOM) Appendix B will specifically verify:

Evidence that a defined organizational structure exists. Surveyors will request the current organizational chart and review it for completeness, clarity, and evidence of Governing Body approval.

Evidence that the Administrator is accountable to the Governing Body. Surveyors will look for a clear line of authority from the Governing Body to the Administrator, documented in the organizational chart and Governing Body minutes.

Evidence that the Clinical Manager has authority over clinical operations. Surveyors will verify that the organizational chart positions the Director of Nursing with direct authority over all clinical services and clinical staff.

Evidence that reporting relationships are understood by staff. Surveyors may interview staff at various levels to confirm they know their supervisor, chain of command, and escalation path.

Evidence that the organizational structure supports the scope of services. Surveyors will assess whether positions and departments exist to support all services the agency claims to provide.

Evidence that the organizational chart is current. Surveyors will compare the chart to actual staff roster and check for recent updates reflecting any changes.

8.3 Common Failure Points

9. References

9.1 Federal Regulations

9.2 CMS Guidance

9.3 State Requirements

9.4 Cross-Referenced Agency Policies

10. Training & Acknowledgment Requirements

10.1 All personnel within the scope of this policy (Section 3) shall receive orientation to the agency's organizational structure during initial onboarding per HR-TA-005. Orientation shall include: (a) review of the current organizational chart; (b) identification of the employee's position, direct supervisor, and chain of command; (c) explanation of how to escalate concerns through the chain of command; (d) identification of the Compliance Officer and the independent compliance reporting pathway.

10.2 All personnel within scope shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix B) within 14 calendar days of the policy effective date, any revision, or new hire/appointment.

10.3 The Administrator shall maintain a tracking log of all policy acknowledgments and report any non-compliance to the Governing Body Chair within 7 calendar days of the acknowledgment deadline. Failure to acknowledge within the required timeframe shall result in written notification with a mandatory completion deadline of 7 additional calendar days.

10.4 When the organizational structure changes, the Administrator shall communicate the change to all affected personnel in writing per Section 6.5.3. Affected employees shall confirm receipt and understanding in writing within 7 calendar days of notification.

11. Version Control

11.1 This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per policy EN-LC-001.

11.2 Only the most current approved version of this policy, as reflected in the policy header, is valid for any operational, compliance, or regulatory purpose. All superseded versions must be archived and clearly marked as "SUPERSEDED — NOT FOR USE."

11.3 Any substantive revision to this policy requires: (a) review and approval by the Governing Body, documented in meeting minutes; (b) re-acknowledgment by all personnel within scope, within 14 calendar days of the revised effective date; (c) update to the enterprise policy index per EN-TG-001.

11.4 Non-substantive revisions (formatting, typographical corrections, updated cross-references) may be approved by the Administrator with notification to the Governing Body at the next regular meeting. Non-substantive revisions do not require re-acknowledgment.

Policy 2 of 7: GV-OG-002

Administrator Qualifications & Responsibilities

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy defines the minimum qualifications, duties, authority, and accountability requirements for the Administrator of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. The Administrator is the individual appointed by the Governing Body who is responsible for the day-to-day management and operation of the home health agency. This policy ensures compliance with 42 CFR § 484.105(b), which requires a home health agency to designate a qualified administrator who is authorized to act on behalf of the governing body and who is responsible for the agency's overall management, including financial operations, personnel administration, and regulatory compliance. This policy also addresses California-specific administrator qualification requirements as established by the California Department of Public Health and the Health Care Access and Information (HCAI) division.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

The Governing Body of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. (as the appointing authority)

The current Administrator

Any individual being considered for appointment as Administrator

The Administrator Designee (GV-OG-005, HR-JD-002)

The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager (as a direct report)

The Compliance Officer

The HR Director (for qualification verification and personnel file maintenance)

This policy does not apply to other agency staff except to the extent that the Administrator's responsibilities establish requirements, standards, or directives that govern their work.

4. Policy Statement

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall at all times have a designated Administrator who has been formally appointed by the Governing Body and who meets all qualification requirements established in this policy, 42 CFR § 484.105(b), and applicable California state law.

4.2 The Administrator shall be authorized by the Governing Body to act on its behalf in the day-to-day management and operation of the agency, subject to the limitations defined in the Delegation of Authority policy (GV-OG-005) and the Governing Body's retained responsibilities (GV-GB-001).

4.3 The Administrator shall be accountable to the Governing Body for all aspects of agency operations including, but not limited to: organizational management, personnel administration, financial management, regulatory compliance, service delivery oversight, and maintenance of the agency's licensure and certification.

4.4 The Administrator shall report directly to the Governing Body and shall provide regular reports on agency operations, financial performance, compliance status, and quality metrics at each quarterly Governing Body meeting, as required by GV-GB-001.

4.5 If the Administrator position becomes vacant, the Governing Body shall appoint an interim Administrator who meets the minimum qualifications within 14 calendar days of the vacancy and shall appoint a permanent Administrator within 90 calendar days, per GV-GB-001, Section 6.5.

4.6 The Governing Body shall conduct or commission an annual performance evaluation of the Administrator, as required by GV-GB-001, Section 6.2.2.4.

4.7 Only the most current approved version of this policy shall be considered valid. Superseded versions must not be used for any operational or compliance purpose.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Minimum Qualifications for the Administrator

6.2 Appointment of the Administrator

6.3 Core Responsibilities of the Administrator

The Administrator of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall fulfill the following responsibilities. While the Administrator may delegate specific tasks in accordance with GV-OG-005, the Administrator retains accountability to the Governing Body for all functions.

6.3.1 — Agency Operations Management

6.3.2 — Personnel Administration

6.3.3 — Financial Management

6.3.4 — Regulatory Compliance and Quality Oversight

6.3.5 — Governing Body Reporting and Communication

6.4 Administrator Performance Evaluation

6.5 Administrator Absence and Succession

6.6 Escalation and Exception Handling

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance & Audit Considerations

8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For

CMS surveyors conducting a standard survey under the State Operations Manual (SOM) Appendix B will specifically verify:

Evidence that an Administrator has been appointed by the Governing Body. Surveyors will review Governing Body minutes for documented appointment.

Evidence that the Administrator meets qualification requirements. Surveyors will review the Administrator's personnel file for education, experience, and background verification.

Evidence that the Administrator is responsible for day-to-day management. Surveyors will look for documented authority, reporting relationships, and evidence of active management oversight.

Evidence that the Administrator reports to the Governing Body. Surveyors will verify reporting relationship through the organizational chart, Governing Body minutes, and interview.

Evidence that the Administrator ensures regulatory compliance. Surveyors will assess the overall compliance posture of the agency as an indicator of administrator effectiveness.

Evidence that a succession plan exists for the Administrator position. Surveyors may inquire about plans for management continuity in the event of an Administrator vacancy.

8.3 Common Failure Points

Orientation shall be conducted by the Governing Body Chair or designated member and shall cover: (a) qualifications and ongoing eligibility requirements; (b) scope of authority and delegation limits; (c) reporting obligations to the Governing Body; (d) financial, compliance, and quality oversight responsibilities; (e) performance evaluation process; (f) absence and succession requirements.

Policy 3 of 7: GV-OG-003

Scope of Services Definition

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy formally defines the range of home health services that Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. is authorized, licensed, certified, and staffed to provide. A clearly defined scope of services is essential to ensure the agency does not accept patients or provide services beyond its capabilities, licensure, or certification. This policy ensures compliance with 42 CFR § 484.105(a), which requires the governing body to assume responsibility for ensuring the agency provides services in accordance with its established scope, and with California HCAI licensure requirements that mandate agencies operate only within the services for which they are licensed. The Governing Body must approve the scope of services annually to ensure ongoing alignment between the agency's authorized services, available competencies, and patient population needs.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

The Governing Body of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc.

The Agency Administrator

The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager

All department heads and clinical supervisors

All intake and admissions staff

All clinical staff involved in service delivery

All referral sources and contracted service providers

This policy does not apply to services provided by other agencies or facilities to which Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. may refer patients. It applies only to services directly provided or arranged by this agency.

4. Policy Statement

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a formally documented scope of services that defines every service the agency is authorized, licensed, certified, staffed, and competent to provide, as required by 42 CFR § 484.105(a) and California home health agency licensure requirements.

4.2 The scope of services shall be approved by the Governing Body annually and shall be reviewed any time there is a change in the agency's licensure, certification, staffing, or service capabilities.

4.3 The agency shall not accept patients requiring services that fall outside its defined scope of services. All intake and admissions personnel must verify that each referred patient's service needs can be met within the scope defined by this policy before accepting the patient for admission, per OP-IM-002.

4.4 The agency shall not provide any service for which it does not hold the required licensure, certification, or qualified staffing. Any expansion or reduction of the scope of services requires prior Governing Body approval and, where applicable, regulatory notification or approval.

4.5 The scope of services shall be communicated to all referral sources, clearly published in the agency's marketing and informational materials, and included in the agency's orientation program for new staff.

4.6 The defined scope of services must be supported by the agency's organizational structure (GV-OG-001) and staffing plan (HR-WM-001) at all times.

4.7 Only the most current approved version of this policy and the scope of services document (Appendix A) shall be considered valid.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Defined Scope of Services

Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. is authorized and provides the following services within its defined scope. This list constitutes the agency's official scope of services and is maintained in detail in Appendix A.

6.1.1 — Core Services (Directly Provided)

6.1.2 — Specialty Services (Directly Provided Based on Staffing Competency)

6.1.3 — Services Not Within Scope

Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. does not provide the following services. Patients requiring these services shall be referred to an appropriate provider:

6.2 Annual Review and Approval of Scope of Services

6.3 Scope of Services Expansion

6.4 Scope of Services Reduction

6.5 Intake Verification Against Scope of Services

6.6 Escalation and Exception Handling

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance & Audit Considerations

8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For

CMS surveyors conducting a standard survey under the State Operations Manual (SOM) Appendix B will specifically verify:

Evidence that the agency has a defined scope of services. Surveyors will request the scope of services document and verify Governing Body approval.

Evidence that the agency provides only services within its defined scope. Surveyors will compare services delivered (from clinical records) against the defined scope.

Evidence that the agency has qualified staff for each service it provides. Surveyors will verify staffing competencies for each service discipline within the scope.

Evidence that the scope of services aligns with licensure and certification. Surveyors will compare the scope to the agency's California license and Medicare certification.

Evidence that intake criteria reference the scope of services. Surveyors may review intake processes to verify that patients are not accepted for services outside the scope.

Training shall include: (a) the current list of core and specialty services; (b) services not within scope; (c) intake verification requirements; (d) how to handle referrals for out-of-scope services.

10.2 All personnel within scope shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix B) within 14 calendar days of the policy effective date, any revision, or new hire.

Policy 4 of 7: GV-OG-004

Strategic Planning & Annual Goals

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy requires the Governing Body and the Administrator of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. to establish, document, and review annual strategic goals and operational objectives that guide the direction of the agency. Strategic planning ensures the agency operates with purpose and direction, aligns resources with priorities, and proactively addresses opportunities and threats in the regulatory, clinical, financial, and operational environment. While CMS Conditions of Participation do not mandate a specific strategic planning process, effective strategic planning is a governance best practice that supports the Governing Body's oversight responsibilities under 42 CFR § 484.105 and is expected by accreditation bodies, OIG compliance guidance, and IBM enterprise governance standards. A defined strategic plan also provides the framework against which the Governing Body evaluates the Administrator's performance (GV-OG-002) and the QAPI program's effectiveness (QA-PG-002).

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

The Governing Body of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc.

The Agency Administrator

The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager

The Compliance Officer

All department heads and senior leadership personnel

The QAPI Coordinator

This policy does not apply to clinical or administrative line staff, except to the extent that strategic goals and operational objectives are communicated to them and reflected in their departmental performance expectations.

4. Policy Statement

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall develop, document, and maintain an annual strategic plan that defines the agency's priorities, goals, and operational objectives for the upcoming year.

4.2 The strategic plan shall be developed under the direction of the Administrator with input from all department heads and presented to the Governing Body for review and approval at the first quarterly meeting of each calendar year or within 30 calendar days of the start of the agency's fiscal year.

4.3 The strategic plan shall include, at minimum: (a) a mission and vision statement; (b) strategic priorities for the planning period; (c) measurable goals with defined timelines and accountable parties; (d) alignment with the QAPI plan (QA-PG-002); (e) alignment with the annual operating budget (FN-FP-005); (f) a risk assessment identifying threats and mitigation strategies.

4.4 The Governing Body shall receive quarterly progress reports on strategic goal achievement and shall direct corrective action when goals are not on track.

4.5 The strategic plan shall be treated as a living document. Material changes to strategic direction require Governing Body approval, documented in meeting minutes.

4.6 Only the most current approved version of the strategic plan shall be considered valid.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Annual Strategic Planning Process

6.2 Quarterly Progress Review

6.3 Strategic Plan Modification

6.4 Alignment with QAPI and Budget

6.5 Escalation and Exception Handling

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance & Audit Considerations

8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For

While CMS standard survey does not specifically require a strategic plan, surveyors may review strategic planning documentation as evidence of governing body engagement and oversight. Accreditation surveyors (if applicable) will specifically look for:

Evidence that the agency has a documented, forward-looking plan that demonstrates purposeful governance.

Evidence that the Governing Body is engaged in setting direction and not merely reacting to events.

Evidence that quality improvement activities are aligned with organizational priorities.

Evidence that financial resources are allocated to support organizational goals.

10.2 All personnel within scope shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix B) within 14 calendar days of the policy effective date, any revision, or new appointment.

10.3 Department heads shall communicate strategic goals relevant to their departments to their teams within 14 calendar days of receiving the approved plan.

Policy 5 of 7: GV-OG-005

Delegation of Authority

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy defines the conditions, limitations, documentation requirements, and accountability mechanisms for delegating administrative, clinical, and operational authority within Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Delegation of authority is necessary to enable efficient day-to-day operations while maintaining clear accountability. However, delegation must be carefully controlled to ensure that the Governing Body retains ultimate accountability for the agency's operation and management as required by 42 CFR § 484.105(a), and that delegated authority is exercised only by qualified individuals acting within defined limits. This policy prevents unauthorized assumption of authority, ensures all delegations are documented and traceable, and establishes the principle that accountability cannot be delegated even when tasks and authority are.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

The Governing Body of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc.

The Agency Administrator

The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager

The Compliance Officer

All department heads, supervisors, and managers who exercise delegated authority

All individuals who have been formally designated as a "designee" for any leadership position (Administrator Designee, Clinical Designee)

This policy does not apply to clinical delegation of nursing tasks (e.g., RN delegation to LVN or HHA), which is governed by the California Nursing Practice Act and agency clinical policies (CL-SD-008, CL-SD-006).

4. Policy Statement

4.1 The Governing Body of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. delegates authority to the Administrator for the day-to-day management of the agency, subject to the retained responsibilities and limitations defined in GV-GB-001. This delegation shall be documented in writing and recorded in Governing Body meeting minutes.

4.2 The Administrator may delegate specific authority to department heads, supervisors, and designees to enable efficient operations, provided that: (a) the delegation is in writing; (b) the delegatee meets minimum qualifications for the delegated function; (c) the scope and limits of the delegation are clearly defined; (d) the delegation includes accountability mechanisms and reporting requirements; (e) the Administrator retains accountability to the Governing Body for all delegated functions.

4.3 The following authorities shall not be delegated by the Governing Body to any individual or entity:

Ultimate legal authority for agency operation and management (42 CFR § 484.105(a))

Appointment of the Administrator, Director of Nursing, and Compliance Officer

Approval of REQUIRED-tier policies

Approval of the annual QAPI plan

Approval of the annual operating budget

Approval of the scope of services

Approval of the emergency preparedness plan

4.4 The following authorities shall not be delegated by the Administrator without explicit Governing Body approval:

Authority to enter into contracts exceeding $25,000

Authority to terminate key leadership personnel

Authority to modify the organizational structure (material changes per GV-OG-001)

Authority to commit the agency to regulatory or legal settlements

Authority to expand or reduce the scope of services

4.5 All delegations of authority shall be documented using the Delegation of Authority Form (Appendix A) and maintained in the agency governance file.

4.6 Delegation does not transfer accountability. The delegating party remains accountable for the outcomes of the delegated function.

4.7 Only the most current approved version of this policy shall be considered valid.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Governing Body Delegation to the Administrator

6.2 Administrator Delegation to Department Heads and Designees

6.3.1 — Administrator Designee

6.5 Revocation of Delegated Authority

6.6 Escalation and Exception Handling

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance & Audit Considerations

8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For

CMS surveyors will verify:

Evidence that the Governing Body has delegated authority to the Administrator in writing. Surveyors will review Governing Body minutes and the delegation documentation.

Evidence that the Governing Body retains ultimate accountability. Surveyors will look for evidence that the Governing Body makes key decisions directly (budget, scope, QAPI plan, key personnel).

Evidence that delegated authority is clearly defined. Surveyors may interview the Administrator and other leaders to confirm understanding of their authority and its limits.

Evidence that designated individuals are qualified. Surveyors will review qualifications for anyone exercising delegated authority, particularly the Administrator Designee.

8.3 Common Failure Points

9. References

9.2 Cross-Referenced Agency Policies

10. Training & Acknowledgment Requirements

10.1 All individuals who exercise delegated authority (Administrator, department heads, designees) shall receive training on this policy at the time of initial delegation and annually thereafter. Training shall cover: (a) the principle that delegation transfers authority but not accountability; (b) retained authorities at each level; (c) documentation requirements; (d) scope and limitations of their specific delegation; (e) monitoring and revocation procedures.

10.2 All personnel within scope shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix C) within 14 calendar days of the policy effective date, any revision, or new appointment.

11. Version Control

11.1 This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per policy EN-LC-001.

11.2 Only the most current approved version of this policy, as reflected in the policy header, is valid for any operational, compliance, or regulatory purpose. All superseded versions must be archived and clearly marked as "SUPERSEDED — NOT FOR USE."

11.3 Any substantive revision requires: (a) review and approval by the Governing Body, documented in meeting minutes; (b) re-acknowledgment by all personnel within scope, within 14 calendar days of the revised effective date; (c) update to the enterprise policy index per EN-TG-001.

11.4 Non-substantive revisions may be approved by the Administrator with notification to the Governing Body at the next regular meeting.

Policy 6 of 7: GV-PM-001

Policy Development & Approval Process

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes the standardized process for developing, reviewing, approving, and disseminating agency policies at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. A consistent, documented policy development process ensures that all agency policies are evidence-based, regulatory-compliant, operationally sound, and approved by the appropriate authority before implementation. CMS Conditions of Participation require that the governing body ensures the development of policies and procedures governing the agency's services (42 CFR § 484.105(a)), and the OIG Compliance Program Guidance requires written standards, policies, and procedures as a foundational element of an effective compliance program. This policy also ensures that the agency's policy framework meets IBM Knowledge Catalog governance artifact standards for lifecycle management, version control, and approval documentation.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

All individuals who develop, draft, review, approve, or disseminate policies for Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc.

The Governing Body (approval of REQUIRED-tier policies)

The Administrator (approval of ESSENTIAL, RECOMMENDED, and GOOD TO HAVE-tier policies)

The Compliance Officer (policy framework governance and quality assurance)

All department heads and Policy Owner/Stewards

All subject matter experts and stakeholders who contribute to policy development

This policy governs all written policies, procedures, and protocols that operate under the enterprise policy taxonomy framework (EN-TG-001). It does not govern informal departmental standard operating procedures (SOPs), clinical standing orders, or physician orders, though these documents must be consistent with approved policies.

4. Policy Statement

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a standardized policy development and approval process that ensures all agency policies are developed systematically, reviewed by appropriate stakeholders, approved by the appropriate authority, and disseminated to all affected personnel before implementation.

4.2 All policies shall be classified within the agency's enterprise policy taxonomy framework per EN-TG-001 and assigned a classification tier (REQUIRED, ESSENTIAL, RECOMMENDED, or GOOD TO HAVE) that determines the approval authority.

4.3 The following approval authorities apply:

4.4 No policy shall be implemented, disseminated, or enforced until it has completed the full development and approval process defined in this policy.

4.5 All policies shall include the IBM-mandated metadata fields defined in the enterprise policy taxonomy framework (EN-TG-001, Section C): Policy ID, Title, Domain, Subdomain, Classification Tier, Status, Review Cycle, Access Tier, Policy Owner/Steward, Effective Date, Version, Approved By, Last Reviewed, Next Review Date, and Supersedes.

4.6 The Compliance Officer shall serve as the enterprise policy framework steward and is responsible for ensuring the integrity, consistency, and quality of the agency's policy library.

4.7 Only the most current approved version of any policy shall be considered valid. Superseded versions must be archived per EN-LC-001.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Policy Initiation

6.2 Policy Drafting

6.4 Approval

6.6 Expedited Policy Development (Emergency)

8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For

CMS surveyors will verify:

Evidence that the agency has a formal policy development and approval process. Surveyors will request this policy (GV-PM-001) and evidence of its application.

Evidence that the Governing Body approves agency policies. Surveyors will review Governing Body minutes for policy approval actions.

Evidence that policies are current and reviewed. Surveyors will check effective dates, review dates, and version numbers.

Evidence that policies are disseminated to staff. Surveyors may ask staff if they are aware of specific policies and how they received them.

Evidence that policies are operationally enforced. Surveyors will compare observed practice against written policies.

Training shall cover: (a) the 11-section template and formatting requirements; (b) the development, review, and approval workflow; (c) IBM metadata requirements; (d) classification tier and approval authority; (e) stakeholder review process; (f) dissemination and acknowledgment requirements.

10.2 All personnel within scope shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix B) within 14 calendar days of the policy effective date, any revision, or new assignment as a Policy Owner/Steward.

Policy 7 of 7: GV-PM-002

Policy Review & Revision Cycle

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy mandates the periodic review and revision of all policies at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. on a defined cycle with documented evidence of review and revision. Policies that are not regularly reviewed become outdated, may not reflect current regulatory requirements, and create compliance risk during CMS surveys and audits. 42 CFR § 484.105 requires the governing body to ensure that the agency's policies and procedures are current and appropriate, and CMS surveyors evaluate whether the agency has a policy review process as part of the standard survey. This policy establishes three review cycle categories (Annual, Biennial, and Triggered) as defined in the enterprise policy taxonomy framework (EN-TG-001) and ensures that all 244 policies in the agency's framework are reviewed within their assigned cycle, with documented evidence that each review was conducted, findings were assessed, and the policy was either reaffirmed or revised.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

All 244 policies in the agency's enterprise policy framework (EN-TG-001)

The Compliance Officer (policy lifecycle governance)

All Policy Owner/Stewards responsible for their assigned policies

The Administrator (approval authority for non-REQUIRED-tier revisions)

The Governing Body (approval authority for REQUIRED-tier revisions and oversight of the review cycle)

All department heads who supervise Policy Owner/Stewards

This policy does not apply to external documents referenced in agency policies (e.g., CMS guidance, regulatory texts) or to informal departmental procedures that are not part of the formal policy framework.

4. Policy Statement

4.1 Every policy in the agency's enterprise policy framework shall be reviewed on a defined cycle. The three review cycles and their definitions are:

4.2 A policy review constitutes a documented assessment by the Policy Owner/Steward that evaluates: (a) whether the policy reflects current federal, state, and local regulations; (b) whether the policy reflects current CMS guidance and interpretive guidelines; (c) whether the policy reflects current agency operations and practices; (d) whether the policy is internally consistent with other agency policies; (e) whether the policy's compliance indicators and common failure points are still accurate; (f) whether any incidents, audit findings, or complaints have identified deficiencies in the policy.

4.3 A review may result in one of two outcomes: (a) reaffirmation (the policy is current and requires no changes) or (b) revision (the policy requires substantive or non-substantive changes). Both outcomes must be documented.

4.4 No policy shall exceed its review cycle deadline by more than 30 calendar days without documented justification and Compliance Officer approval for an extension.

4.5 The Compliance Officer shall maintain a Policy Review Calendar (Appendix A) that tracks the review status of all 244 policies and ensures timely completion of all reviews.

4.6 The Governing Body shall receive an annual summary report on the status of the policy review cycle at the first quarterly meeting of each calendar year.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Policy Review Calendar Management

6.2 Conducting a Policy Review

6.3 Reaffirmation (No Revision Needed)

6.4 Revision Process

6.5 Triggered Reviews

6.6 Annual Reporting to the Governing Body

6.7 Escalation and Exception Handling

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance & Audit Considerations

8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For

CMS surveyors will verify:

Evidence that the agency has a defined policy review process. Surveyors will request this policy (GV-PM-002) and the Policy Review Calendar.

Evidence that policies are current. Surveyors will check Last Reviewed dates on policies they select for review. An outdated policy (reviewed more than 12–24 months ago depending on cycle) is a common finding.

Evidence that reviews result in documented action. Surveyors may review Policy Review Worksheets to verify that reviews are substantive assessments and not mere "check the box" exercises.

Evidence that the Governing Body oversees the policy review process. Surveyors will look for Governing Body minutes documenting receipt of the annual policy review report and approval of revised REQUIRED-tier policies.

Evidence that regulatory changes trigger policy updates. Surveyors may ask whether a recent CMS rule change (e.g., OASIS-E2 updates) has been incorporated into affected policies.

8.3 Common Failure Points

9. References

9.1 Federal Regulations

9.2 Industry Standards

9.3 Cross-Referenced Agency Policies

10. Training & Acknowledgment Requirements

10.1 All Policy Owner/Stewards shall receive training on this policy and the policy review process at the time of their first policy assignment and annually thereafter. Training shall cover: (a) review cycle definitions and deadlines; (b) how to conduct a policy review; (c) completing the Policy Review Worksheet; (d) when to reaffirm vs. revise; (e) the triggered review process; (f) escalation procedures for overdue reviews.

10.2 All personnel within scope shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix C) within 14 calendar days of the policy effective date, any revision, or new assignment.

10.3 The Compliance Officer shall include policy review cycle compliance in the annual compliance training program per CO-CP-008.

11. Version Control

11.1 This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per policy EN-LC-001.

11.2 Only the most current approved version of this policy, as reflected in the policy header, is valid for any operational, compliance, or regulatory purpose. All superseded versions must be archived and clearly marked as "SUPERSEDED — NOT FOR USE."

11.3 Any substantive revision to this policy requires: (a) review and approval by the Governing Body, documented in meeting minutes; (b) re-acknowledgment by all personnel within scope, within 14 calendar days of the revised effective date; (c) update to the enterprise policy index per EN-TG-001.

11.4 Non-substantive revisions may be approved by the Compliance Officer with notification to the Administrator and the Governing Body at the next regular meeting.

GV-PM-003 — Policy Acknowledgment & Staff Attestation

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes the requirements for documented acknowledgment and attestation by all workforce members upon the issuance, revision, or assignment of agency policies. Acknowledgment ensures that all individuals subject to a policy have received, read, and understood their obligations under that policy. This policy supports the agency's compliance with CMS Conditions of Participation, OIG Compliance Program Guidance, and California state employment and licensing requirements by creating an auditable record of workforce policy awareness and accountability.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

All employees of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. (full-time, part-time, and per diem)

All contracted clinical and non-clinical staff performing services on behalf of the agency

All members of the Governing Body

All students, interns, and volunteers functioning within the agency

All agency leadership, including the Administrator, Director of Nursing, and Compliance Officer

This policy does not apply to external vendors or business associates who are not directly performing services under agency supervision, except where a specific policy expressly requires their acknowledgment.

4. Policy Statement

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall require documented acknowledgment of all agency policies by all individuals within scope of each policy, as a condition of employment, contract, and Governing Body membership.

4.2 Policy acknowledgment shall occur:

Within 14 calendar days of initial hire or new appointment for all policies applicable to the individual's role

Within 14 calendar days of the effective date of any new policy applicable to the individual's role

Within 14 calendar days of the effective date of any substantive revision to an existing applicable policy

Within 14 calendar days of any role change that expands the scope of policies applicable to the individual

4.3 Acknowledgment shall be documented using the standardized Policy Acknowledgment Form (see Appendix A of the applicable policy, or the general acknowledgment form in Appendix A of this policy). Electronic acknowledgment through the agency's designated platform is an acceptable alternative to paper forms, provided the system captures the individual's identity, date, and a confirmation of receipt and understanding.

4.4 The Administrator shall maintain a centralized policy acknowledgment tracking log for all agency policies and all individuals within scope. This log shall be current at all times and available for CMS survey review.

4.5 Non-compliance with acknowledgment requirements shall be escalated per Section 6.4 of this policy. Failure to acknowledge assigned policies within required timeframes may result in corrective action, up to and including suspension from patient care duties pending completion.

4.6 Acknowledgment of a policy does not substitute for training. Where a policy requires training in addition to acknowledgment, both requirements must be independently satisfied and documented.

4.7 Governing Body members and senior leadership shall acknowledge all REQUIRED-tier and Tier 4 — Privileged policies within 14 calendar days of appointment and within 14 calendar days of any revision.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Policy Assignment and Acknowledgment Trigger Events

6.2 Acknowledgment Completion

6.3 Acknowledgment Tracking and Reporting

6.4 Non-Compliance and Escalation

6.5 Acknowledgment During Leaves of Absence

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance & Audit Considerations

8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For

CMS surveyors and OIG auditors will specifically examine:

Evidence that workforce members have acknowledged the policies governing their scope of practice and compliance obligations, particularly REQUIRED-tier clinical, compliance, and patient safety policies.

Evidence that the Governing Body has acknowledged all REQUIRED-tier governance policies, including this policy.

Currency and completeness of the Acknowledgment Tracking Log.

Evidence that non-compliance with acknowledgment requirements is tracked and acted upon.

Consistency between the agency's stated acknowledgment requirements (in individual policy documents) and the tracking system maintained by the Administrator.

8.3 Common Failure Points

9. References

9.1 Federal Regulations

9.2 OIG Guidance

9.3 Cross-Referenced Agency Policies

10. Training & Acknowledgment Requirements

10.1 All individuals within the scope of this policy shall receive orientation to the acknowledgment process as part of new employee orientation or Governing Body onboarding, conducted by the Administrator or designee.

10.2 All individuals within scope shall acknowledge this policy (GV-PM-003) within 14 calendar days of their effective date of hire, appointment, or this policy's effective date.

10.3 Annual refresher on acknowledgment obligations shall be incorporated into the agency's annual mandatory training program per policy HR-TD-001.

11. Version Control

11.1 This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per policy EN-LC-001.

11.2 Only the most current approved version of this policy is valid for any operational, compliance, or regulatory purpose.

11.3 Any substantive revision requires Governing Body approval (documented in meeting minutes), re-acknowledgment by all personnel within scope within 14 calendar days, and update to the enterprise policy index per EN-TG-001.

GV-PM-004 — Communication & Notification Standards

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes the standards governing internal and external communication and notification at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Effective communication is essential to patient safety, regulatory compliance, operational continuity, and workforce accountability. This policy defines timeliness requirements, acceptable communication channels, escalation protocols, and documentation obligations for all categories of organizational communication, ensuring that critical information reaches the appropriate individuals in a reliable, accurate, and auditable manner.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

All employees of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. at all levels

All contracted clinical and non-clinical personnel performing services on behalf of the agency

The Administrator, Director of Nursing, Compliance Officer, and all department leads

The Governing Body, with respect to notifications directed to or from the Governing Body

All communications involving patients, families, referral sources, payers, and regulatory bodies

This policy does not govern clinical documentation standards (see CL-CD-001) or HIPAA-specific privacy and security requirements for PHI communications (see CO-HP-001, CO-HP-002), which are addressed in their respective policies but must be read in conjunction with this policy.

4. Policy Statement

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain clear, timely, and documented communication channels at all organizational levels to support patient safety, compliance, and operational effectiveness.

4.2 All communications that require action, document a material decision, or affect patient care or regulatory compliance shall be documented in writing (paper or electronic) and retained per the agency's record retention requirements in policy CO-HP-007.

4.3 Verbal communications regarding patient care, compliance concerns, or operational decisions shall be confirmed in writing within the timeframes specified in Section 6 of this policy.

4.4 All communications involving PHI shall comply with HIPAA privacy and security requirements per policies CO-HP-001 and CO-HP-002. PHI shall not be transmitted via unsecured channels, including personal email or unencrypted text messaging, without explicit patient authorization or a documented operational emergency.

4.5 The agency shall maintain an escalation protocol ensuring that urgent clinical, compliance, and regulatory matters are communicated to the appropriate leadership level without delay. No individual shall impede or delay the escalation of a patient safety or compliance concern.

4.6 Regulatory agencies, accrediting bodies, and government authorities shall receive all required notifications within the timeframes mandated by applicable law or regulation, and responses shall be coordinated through the Administrator with oversight from the Compliance Officer.

4.7 All staff are obligated to communicate concerns about patient safety, compliance, or operational risk through established channels and are protected from retaliation for doing so per policy CO-CP-005.

GV-PM-005 — Stakeholder Grievance & Feedback Management

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes the process for receiving, documenting, investigating, resolving, and trending grievances and feedback from patients, families, staff, referral sources, and other stakeholders of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. A robust grievance and feedback management program supports patient rights, workforce engagement, quality improvement, and regulatory compliance. This policy integrates with the agency's QAPI program and patient rights framework to ensure that all concerns are treated seriously, addressed promptly, and used to drive continuous improvement.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

All patients receiving services from Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc.

All family members, legal representatives, and caregivers acting on behalf of patients

All agency employees and contracted staff

Referral sources, physicians, discharge planners, and care coordination partners

Community members or organizations with concerns about agency practices

All agency leadership, including the Administrator, Director of Nursing, and Compliance Officer

This policy applies to all types of grievances and feedback, including those received in person, by telephone, in writing, electronically, or through third parties (e.g., regulatory hotlines, ombudsman offices).

4. Policy Statement

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain an accessible, non-retaliatory, and responsive grievance and feedback management process that ensures all concerns from patients, families, staff, and other stakeholders are received, documented, investigated, and resolved in a timely and respectful manner.

4.2 Patients and families shall be informed of their right to file a grievance and the process for doing so at the time of admission, per policy CL-PR-001 (Patient Rights & Responsibilities), and shall not be subject to retaliation, discrimination, or changes in care as a result of filing a grievance.

4.3 All grievances shall be acknowledged within 5 business days of receipt and resolved or formally responded to within 30 calendar days of receipt, unless the nature of the grievance requires a longer investigation, in which case interim status updates shall be provided every 14 calendar days.

4.4 Staff grievances and complaints shall be received through the process defined in this policy and in policy HR-ER-003 (Employee Grievance & Complaint Process). Staff shall not be subject to retaliation for filing a good-faith grievance, per policy CO-CP-005.

4.5 All grievances and feedback shall be logged in the agency's Grievance and Feedback Register and trended quarterly as part of the QAPI program (policy QA-PG-001) to identify systemic issues and opportunities for improvement.

4.6 Grievances alleging abuse, neglect, exploitation, or HIPAA violations shall be immediately escalated to the Compliance Officer and handled per their respective specialized policies (CL-PR-006, CO-HP-003).

4.7 The Administrator shall report grievance volume, resolution rates, and trend data to the Governing Body at each quarterly meeting as part of the operational oversight report.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Receiving and Logging Grievances

6.2 Triage and Escalation

6.3 Investigation and Resolution

6.4 Staff Grievances
