POLICY: RM-ER-002 — Incident Reporting & Investigation

Policy Header

1. Purpose

This policy establishes the requirements for reporting, documenting, and investigating all incidents, near-misses, and adverse events occurring in connection with the operations of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. A robust incident reporting system is essential for identifying risks, preventing recurrence, improving patient and staff safety, and supporting compliance with 42 CFR Part 484, OSHA requirements, and state mandatory reporting obligations.

2. Scope

This policy applies to:

All employees of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. (clinical and administrative)

All contracted and per diem staff providing services on behalf of the agency

All supervisory and management personnel

All volunteers performing activities under agency direction

The Risk Manager, Administrator, Director of Nursing, and Compliance Officer

3. Definitions

4. Policy Statements

4.1 All employees, contractors, and volunteers of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall immediately report any incident, adverse event, near miss, or unsafe condition through the agency's incident reporting system.

4.2 The agency shall maintain a no-retaliation policy for good-faith incident reporting. No employee shall face disciplinary action for reporting an incident, per policy CO-CP-005.

4.3 Incident reports are confidential risk management documents. They shall not be filed in the patient's clinical record and shall be maintained in the risk management file.

4.4 All incidents shall be classified by severity level and investigated according to a tiered investigation protocol proportional to severity.

4.5 Mandatory external reporting obligations (to state agencies, CMS, law enforcement, adult protective services) shall be fulfilled within the timeframes required by applicable law, regardless of internal investigation status.

4.6 All sentinel events shall trigger an immediate investigation and root cause analysis per policy QA-AE-002.

4.7 Incident data shall be aggregated, trended, and reported to the Risk Management Committee quarterly per RM-ER-005, and to the QAPI Committee per QA-PG-003.

5. Procedures

5.1 Immediate Response

5.2 Incident Report Completion

5.3 Incident Classification

5.4 Investigation Process

5.5 Mandatory External Reporting

5.6 Corrective Action and Follow-Up

5.7 Trending and Analysis

6. Documentation Requirements

7. Compliance Monitoring and Measurement

Common Failure Points

8. Regulatory References

Cross-Referenced Policies

9. Training Requirements

9.1 All new employees shall receive incident reporting training during orientation, within 14 calendar days of hire, covering: (a) what constitutes a reportable incident; (b) how to complete the Incident Report Form; (c) to whom and when to report; (d) non-retaliation protections; (e) distinction between incident report and clinical documentation.

9.2 All staff shall receive annual refresher training on incident reporting.

9.3 All supervisory staff shall receive additional training on: (a) Incident Report review and completion oversight; (b) immediate response and escalation protocols; (c) evidence preservation.

9.4 The Risk Manager and Investigation Team members shall receive training on investigation methodology and root cause analysis.

9.5 All in-scope personnel shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix G) within 14 calendar days of effective date, revision, or new hire.

10. Version Control

Per RM-ER-001 §10. Only the most current approved version is valid.

POLICY: RM-ER-003 — Risk Assessment & Prioritization

Policy Header

1. Purpose

This policy mandates the conduct of regular, systematic risk assessments across all operational domains of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Risk assessments provide the foundation for informed decision-making, resource allocation, and risk mitigation by identifying, scoring, and prioritizing risks based on likelihood and severity of impact.

2. Scope

This policy applies to the Risk Manager, all department directors, the Administrator, the Risk Management Committee, and all personnel responsible for conducting or contributing to risk assessments.

3. Definitions

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall conduct a comprehensive enterprise-wide risk assessment annually.

4.2 Targeted risk assessments shall be conducted within 72 hours of any triggering event as defined in RM-ER-001 §5.2.5.

4.3 All risk assessments shall use the agency's standardized Risk Assessment Matrix (RM-ER-001, Appendix A) to ensure consistency.

4.4 Department directors shall participate in the annual comprehensive risk assessment by identifying and submitting domain-specific risks.

4.5 All assessed risks shall be documented in the centralized Risk Register per RM-ER-001.

4.6 Risk prioritization shall directly inform the agency's mitigation planning, resource allocation, and strategic planning processes.

5. Procedures

5.2 Targeted Risk Assessments

5.3 Quarterly Risk Portfolio Review

POLICY: RM-ER-004 — Liability & Insurance Management

Policy Header

1. Purpose

This policy establishes requirements for maintaining adequate insurance coverage as a core risk transfer strategy within the ERM framework of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Appropriate insurance coverage protects the agency, its patients, staff, and governing body from financial loss resulting from liability claims, property damage, and other insurable risks.

2. Scope

This policy applies to the Governing Body, Administrator, Risk Manager, CFO/Revenue Cycle Director, and any personnel involved in insurance procurement, claims management, or risk transfer decisions.

3. Definitions

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain current and adequate insurance coverage as a fundamental component of its enterprise risk management strategy.

4.2 The following insurance coverage types shall be maintained at minimum:

(a) Professional liability (malpractice) insurance

(b) General liability insurance

(c) Workers' compensation insurance (per California state law)

(d) Commercial auto insurance (for agency-owned or leased vehicles, if applicable)

(e) Cyber liability insurance

(f) Directors & Officers liability insurance (if the Governing Body includes a board of directors)

4.3 Coverage levels shall be reviewed annually by the Risk Manager and Administrator to ensure adequacy based on current risk exposure, agency size, service volume, and industry benchmarks.

4.4 The Governing Body shall approve insurance coverage levels annually as part of the budget approval process per FN-FP-005.

4.5 No lapse in required insurance coverage shall occur. The Risk Manager shall monitor all policy expiration dates and initiate renewal no later than 90 calendar days before expiration.

4.6 All contracted and per diem staff shall provide evidence of current professional liability insurance coverage prior to providing services per HR-WM-002.

5. Procedures

5.1 Insurance Program Management

5.2 Contractor Insurance Verification

5.3 Claims Notification and Management

6. Documentation Requirements

7. Compliance Monitoring and Measurement

8. Regulatory References

Cross-Referenced Policies

9. Training Requirements

9.1 The Risk Manager shall maintain current knowledge of insurance products, claims management, and liability risk mitigation.

9.2 The Administrator and CFO shall receive annual briefing on insurance coverage, claims status, and adequacy review findings.

9.3 All in-scope personnel shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix D) within 14 calendar days.

10. Version Control

Per RM-ER-001 §10.

POLICY: RM-ER-005 — Risk Trending & Pattern Analysis

Policy Header

1. Purpose

This policy mandates systematic analysis of risk, incident, and adverse event data to identify trends, patterns, and systemic issues requiring proactive intervention. Trending and pattern analysis transforms raw data into actionable intelligence that supports evidence-based risk mitigation and quality improvement.

2. Scope

This policy applies to the Risk Manager, QAPI Coordinator, Risk Management Committee, and all personnel who generate, collect, or analyze risk-related data.

3. Definitions

4. Policy Statements

4.1 The Risk Manager shall conduct monthly trending analysis of all incident and risk data.

4.2 Quarterly trending reports shall be presented to the Risk Management Committee, QAPI Committee, and Governing Body per RM-ER-001.

4.3 Any identified cluster (3+ similar events within 30 days) shall trigger an immediate investigation and escalation per §5.3.

4.4 Trending data shall directly inform risk assessment priorities, mitigation planning, training needs identification, and QAPI project selection.

4.5 Both leading and lagging indicators shall be monitored to enable proactive risk mitigation.

5. Procedures

5.1 Data Collection and Aggregation

5.2 Trending Analysis

5.3 Cluster Identification and Escalation

5.4 Reporting and Integration

6. Documentation Requirements

7. Compliance Monitoring and Measurement

8. Regulatory References and Cross-Referenced Policies

9. Training & Version Control

POLICY: RM-ER-006 — Claims Management & Litigation Support

Policy Header

1. Purpose

This policy establishes procedures for managing liability claims, coordinating with legal counsel, preserving evidence, and supporting litigation defense for Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Effective claims management minimizes financial exposure, protects the agency's reputation, and ensures compliance with legal and insurance requirements.

2. Scope

This policy applies to the Risk Manager, Administrator, Compliance Officer, Governing Body, legal counsel, insurance carriers, and any personnel involved in claims-related activities or litigation support.

3. Definitions

4. Policy Statements

4.1 All claims, demand letters, lawsuits, subpoenas, and notices of potential claims received by any agency employee shall be immediately forwarded to the Risk Manager.

4.2 The Risk Manager shall notify the applicable insurance carrier(s) within 24 hours of receiving any claim or notice of potential claim per RM-ER-004.

4.3 A litigation hold shall be issued within 24 hours of receiving any lawsuit, demand letter, or credible notice of potential litigation.

4.4 No agency employee shall discuss claims, litigation, or potential litigation with any external party (including claimants, their attorneys, or media) without authorization from the Risk Manager or legal counsel.

4.5 The Governing Body shall be notified of all claims and lawsuits per GV-GB-001 §6.5.

4.6 All claims management activities shall be coordinated with the agency's legal counsel per GV-EA-003.

5. Procedures

5.1 Claims Receipt and Initial Response

5.2 Litigation Hold and Evidence Preservation

5.3 Claims Investigation and Coordination

5.4 Resolution and Closure

6. Documentation Requirements

7. Compliance Monitoring and Measurement

8. Regulatory References and Cross-Referenced Policies

9. Training Requirements

9.1 All agency employees shall receive training during orientation on: (a) the obligation to immediately forward any claim or legal document to the Risk Manager; (b) the prohibition against discussing claims with external parties.

9.2 All supervisory personnel shall receive additional training on evidence preservation and litigation hold procedures.

9.3 All in-scope personnel shall sign Appendix C within 14 calendar days.

10. Version Control

Per RM-ER-001 §10.

SUBDOMAIN: RM-SS — STAFF SAFETY

POLICY: RM-SS-001 — Staff Safety & Personal Security

Policy Header

1. Purpose

This policy defines protocols for staff safety during home visits, including threat assessment, communication check-ins, and high-risk visit procedures for Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. The safety of staff providing services in uncontrolled home environments is paramount and requires proactive safety planning, clear communication protocols, and immediate response capabilities.

2. Scope

This policy applies to all employees, contracted staff, and per diem personnel of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. who provide services in patient homes or travel for agency business, as well as supervisory personnel responsible for staff deployment and scheduling.

3. Definitions

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a comprehensive staff safety program that protects all personnel during home health visits and agency travel.

4.2 A Home Visit Safety Assessment shall be conducted for every new patient prior to or at the time of the first visit, and updated whenever safety conditions change.

4.3 All field staff shall follow the agency's Check-In Protocol during patient visits. No staff member shall make a home visit without notifying the agency of their location and expected return.

4.4 Visits shall not be conducted when the staff member's safety is in imminent danger. Staff have the right and obligation to leave a home immediately if they feel unsafe.

4.5 High-risk visits shall require enhanced safety measures including the buddy system, specific check-in intervals, and supervisor notification.

4.6 All staff shall receive initial and annual training on personal safety, de-escalation techniques, and emergency response procedures.

4.7 All safety incidents involving staff shall be reported per RM-ER-002 and investigated.

5. Procedures

5.1 Home Visit Safety Assessment

5.2 Check-In Protocol

5.3 High-Risk Visit Procedures

5.4 Duress Communication

5.5 Post-Incident Response

6. Documentation Requirements

7. Compliance Monitoring and Measurement

Common Failure Points

8. Regulatory References

Cross-Referenced Policies

9. Training Requirements

9.1 All field staff shall receive initial safety training within 14 calendar days of hire covering: (a) Home Visit Safety Assessment; (b) Check-In Protocol; (c) High-Risk Visit procedures; (d) Duress code and Safe Zone; (e) De-escalation techniques; (f) Right to leave unsafe situations; (g) Incident reporting.

9.2 Annual refresher training shall be provided to all field staff.

9.3 All in-scope personnel shall sign Appendix C within 14 calendar days.

10. Version Control

POLICY: RM-SS-002 — Workplace Violence Prevention

Policy Header

1. Purpose

This policy establishes Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc.'s workplace violence prevention program, including risk assessment, reporting protocols, response procedures, and staff protection measures. Home health workers face elevated violence risk due to the uncontrolled home environment, and this policy provides a comprehensive prevention and response framework in compliance with Cal/OSHA workplace violence prevention standards (SB 553).

2. Scope

This policy applies to all employees, contractors, per diem staff, and volunteers of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. It covers all work settings including patient homes, the agency office, community locations, and while in transit.

3. Definitions

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. maintains a zero-tolerance policy for workplace violence. No acts of violence, threats, intimidation, harassment, or bullying will be tolerated from any person — employee, patient, family member, visitor, or third party.

4.2 All staff shall immediately report any incident of workplace violence, threat, or intimidation per RM-ER-002 and this policy.

4.3 No employee shall be retaliated against for reporting workplace violence in good faith, per CO-CP-005.

4.4 The agency shall maintain a written Workplace Violence Prevention Plan (WVPP) as required by California SB 553, effective July 1, 2024.

4.5 Threat assessments shall be conducted for all reported credible threats by the Risk Manager within 24 hours.

4.6 All staff shall receive initial and annual workplace violence prevention training.

5. Procedures

5.2 Incident Reporting and Response

5.3 Investigation and Follow-Up

5.4 Post-Incident Review

POLICY: RM-SS-003 — Motor Vehicle Safety & Accident Reporting

Policy Header

1. Purpose

This policy establishes standards for motor vehicle safety, driving eligibility, accident reporting, and investigation procedures for all personnel of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. who operate motor vehicles for agency business. Home health services require extensive driving in variable conditions, and motor vehicle accidents represent a significant risk to staff safety, patient service continuity, agency liability, and insurance costs.

2. Scope

This policy applies to:

All employees of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. who use personal vehicles or agency-owned/leased vehicles for agency business

All contracted and per diem staff who drive to patient homes or other locations for agency services

All supervisory and management personnel responsible for staff deployment

The Risk Manager, HR Director, and Administrator

3. Definitions

4. Policy Statements

4.1 All personnel who drive for agency business shall maintain a valid driver's license appropriate for the vehicle operated and carry minimum automobile insurance coverage as required by California state law.

4.2 The agency shall verify the motor vehicle record (MVR) of all personnel who drive for agency business at the time of hire and annually thereafter.

4.3 All motor vehicle accidents occurring during agency business shall be reported immediately per the procedures in this policy and documented per RM-ER-002.

4.4 The use of handheld electronic devices while operating a motor vehicle for agency business is strictly prohibited, consistent with California Vehicle Code § 23123 and § 23123.5.

4.5 All personnel shall comply with all applicable traffic laws, wear seatbelts at all times, and operate vehicles in a safe and defensive manner.

4.6 Personnel who fail to maintain driving eligibility or who demonstrate unsafe driving practices shall be restricted from driving for agency business.

4.7 Agency-owned or leased vehicles (if applicable) shall be maintained in safe operating condition with documented maintenance records.

5. Procedures

5.1 Driving Eligibility and Verification

5.2 Safe Driving Standards

5.3 Motor Vehicle Accident Response

5.4 Accident Investigation

5.5 Agency Vehicle Management (If Applicable)

6. Documentation Requirements

7. Compliance Monitoring and Measurement

7.1 Compliance Indicators

7.2 Surveyor Expectations

CMS surveyors may review staff safety measures including transportation safety during survey of 42 CFR § 484.105 (organization and administration). Surveyors will verify:

Evidence that the agency has established vehicle safety standards for staff

Evidence of training on safe driving practices

Evidence that motor vehicle accidents are reported, investigated, and trended

Integration of motor vehicle accident data into the agency's QAPI and risk management programs

7.3 Common Failure Points

8. Regulatory References

Cross-Referenced Policies

9. Training Requirements

9.1 All personnel who drive for agency business shall receive motor vehicle safety training within 14 calendar days of hire covering: (a) safe driving standards; (b) pre-trip vehicle inspection; (c) distracted driving prohibition; (d) accident response procedures; (e) reporting requirements; (f) obligation to report license/insurance changes.

9.2 Annual refresher training shall be provided to all driving staff.

9.3 Additional remedial driving safety training shall be required for any employee involved in a preventable accident.

9.4 All in-scope personnel shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix D) within 14 calendar days.

10. Version Control

Per RM-ER-001 §10. Only the most current approved version is valid.

SUBDOMAIN: RM-PS — PATIENT & ENVIRONMENTAL SAFETY

POLICY: RM-PS-001 — Environmental Safety Assessment

Policy Header

1. Purpose

This policy establishes requirements for assessing and documenting the home environment for safety hazards that may affect patient health, safety, and clinical outcomes for Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Home health services are delivered in uncontrolled environments where hazards—including structural deficiencies, fire risks, infection risks, fall hazards, and environmental contaminants—may compromise patient and staff safety. Systematic environmental assessment enables identification, documentation, patient/caregiver education, and mitigation of hazards to the extent possible.

2. Scope

This policy applies to all clinical staff of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. who provide services in patient homes, including registered nurses, licensed vocational nurses, physical therapists, occupational therapists, speech-language pathologists, medical social workers, home health aides, and their supervisors.

3. Definitions

4. Policy Statements

4.1 An Environmental Safety Assessment shall be completed for every patient at the time of admission (SOC/ROC) and documented in the clinical record.

4.2 Environmental safety shall be reassessed at each recertification, upon any reported change in the home environment, upon any safety incident, and as clinically indicated.

4.3 All identified hazards shall be documented, discussed with the patient/caregiver, and addressed through education, intervention, or referral to the extent possible.

4.4 If a hazard cannot be mitigated and creates an imminent risk to patient safety, the clinician shall notify the supervisor immediately and the agency shall determine whether services can safely continue.

4.5 Environmental Safety Assessment findings shall be communicated to all disciplines providing care in the home.

4.6 Environmental safety data shall be aggregated and reported to the QAPI Committee and Risk Management Committee quarterly for trending analysis.

5. Procedures

5.1 Initial Environmental Safety Assessment

5.2 Ongoing Environmental Safety Monitoring

5.3 Environmental Safety Referrals

5.4 Data Aggregation and Reporting

6. Documentation Requirements

7. Compliance Monitoring and Measurement

Common Failure Points

8. Regulatory References

Cross-Referenced Policies

9. Training Requirements

9.1 All clinical staff shall receive training on environmental safety assessment during orientation within 14 calendar days of hire.

9.2 Annual refresher training on environmental safety assessment, including common hazards, documentation requirements, and escalation procedures.

9.3 All in-scope personnel shall sign Appendix C within 14 calendar days.

10. Version Control

Per RM-ER-001 §10.

POLICY: RM-PS-002 — Hazardous Materials & Waste Management

Policy Header

1. Purpose

This policy defines procedures for the safe handling, storage, transport, and disposal of biohazardous materials, sharps, pharmaceutical waste, and other regulated medical waste generated during home health service delivery by Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Compliance with OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens Standard, California Medical Waste Management Act, and EPA regulations is required to protect staff, patients, and the community.

2. Scope

This policy applies to all clinical staff, home health aides, and any personnel who handle, transport, or dispose of medical waste, sharps, biohazardous materials, or pharmaceutical waste during agency operations.

3. Definitions

4. Policy Statements

4.1 All staff shall follow Standard Precautions when handling blood, body fluids, or other potentially infectious materials per CL-SD-016 and OSHA 29 CFR § 1910.1030.

4.2 Sharps shall be disposed of immediately after use in an approved sharps container at the point of use. Recapping of needles is prohibited.

4.3 Biohazardous waste generated in the patient's home shall be managed and disposed of in compliance with California Medical Waste Management Act (Health & Safety Code § 117600 et seq.) and agency procedures.

4.4 All staff shall have access to appropriate PPE and shall be trained on its proper use, removal, and disposal.

4.5 Exposure incidents shall be reported and managed per the agency's Exposure Control Plan and RM-ER-002.

4.6 Pharmaceutical waste shall be disposed of per FDA and EPA guidelines, with controlled substances disposed of per DEA requirements.

5. Procedures

5.1 Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)

5.2 Sharps Management

5.3 Biohazardous Waste Management

5.4 Pharmaceutical Waste Disposal

5.5 Exposure Incident Response

6. Documentation Requirements

7. Compliance Monitoring and Measurement

Common Failure Points

8. Regulatory References

Cross-Referenced Policies

9. Training Requirements

9.1 All clinical staff shall receive Bloodborne Pathogens training within 14 calendar days of hire and annually thereafter per OSHA 29 CFR § 1910.1030(g)(2).

9.2 Training shall cover: (a) OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens Standard; (b) agency Exposure Control Plan; (c) PPE selection, use, removal, and disposal; (d) sharps safety; (e) biohazardous waste handling; (f) pharmaceutical waste disposal; (g) exposure incident response; (h) Hepatitis B vaccination availability.

9.3 All in-scope personnel shall sign Appendix C within 14 calendar days.

POLICY: RM-PS-003 — Product & Equipment Safety Recall Management

Policy Header

1. Purpose

This policy defines procedures for monitoring, responding to, and documenting medical product, medical device, and equipment safety recalls and alerts affecting patients or operations of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Timely identification and response to recalls protects patients from harm due to defective products and ensures regulatory compliance.

2. Scope

This policy applies to the Risk Manager, Operations Director, Director of Nursing, all clinical staff, and all personnel responsible for procuring, distributing, or using medical products, devices, or equipment on behalf of the agency.

3. Definitions

4. Policy Statements

4.1 The Risk Manager shall monitor FDA recall and safety alert databases weekly to identify recalls that may affect agency operations or patients.

4.2 Upon identification of a recall affecting agency products or patient-in-use products, the agency shall respond according to the recall classification and urgency per the procedures in this policy.

4.3 All Class I recalls affecting products in agency possession or patient use shall be treated as emergent and responded to within 24 hours.

4.4 All recall actions shall be documented in the Recall Tracking Log (Appendix A) and retained for a minimum of 7 years.

4.5 Products subject to recall shall be immediately removed from use, segregated, and labeled "DO NOT USE — RECALL" pending disposition per manufacturer/FDA instructions.

POLICY: RM-PS-004 — Patient Elopement & Wandering Risk

Policy Header

1. Purpose

This policy defines risk assessment and intervention protocols for patients at risk of elopement or unsafe wandering served by Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Patients with cognitive impairment, dementia, delirium, behavioral health conditions, or developmental disabilities may be at risk of leaving their home environment unsafely, resulting in injury, exposure, or death. Systematic identification, documentation, and care planning reduce this risk.

2. Scope

This policy applies to all clinical staff who assess, plan, and deliver care to patients with identified or suspected elopement/wandering risk, their supervisors, and the Director of Nursing.

3. Definitions

4. Policy Statements

4.1 All patients shall be screened for elopement/wandering risk at SOC/ROC as part of the comprehensive assessment.

4.2 Patients identified as at risk shall have an individualized Wandering/Elopement Safety Plan documented in the plan of care.

4.3 Caregivers of at-risk patients shall be educated on elopement prevention strategies, monitoring techniques, and emergency response.

4.4 Elopement events shall be reported per RM-ER-002 and investigated.

4.5 The agency shall not physically restrain patients per CL-PR-004 but shall implement environmental, educational, and monitoring interventions.

POLICY: RM-PS-005 — High-Risk Medication Safety

Policy Header

1. Purpose

This policy establishes enhanced safety protocols for the management of high-risk medications in the home health setting by Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. High-risk medications, including anticoagulants, opioids, insulin, and other agents with narrow therapeutic indices, carry an elevated potential for serious harm if not properly managed. This policy ensures patient safety through structured assessment, monitoring, education, and coordination.

2. Scope

This policy applies to all clinical staff who assess, administer, manage, or educate patients regarding high-risk medications, including registered nurses, licensed vocational nurses, therapists contributing to medication management, and their supervisors.

3. Definitions

4. Policy Statements

4.1 The agency shall maintain a list of designated high-risk/high-alert medications based on the ISMP List of High-Alert Medications in Community/Ambulatory Settings, updated annually.

4.2 Enhanced safety protocols shall be applied to all patients receiving high-risk medications, including increased assessment frequency, structured monitoring parameters, patient/caregiver education, and documented safety checks.

4.3 All medication adverse events involving high-risk medications shall be reported per RM-ER-002 and QA-AE-001.

4.4 The agency shall maintain competency requirements for all clinical staff involved in high-risk medication management.

4.5 High-risk medication safety data shall be monitored and reported to the QAPI Committee quarterly.

POLICY: RM-EP-001 — Pandemic & Infectious Disease Response

Policy Header

1. Purpose

This policy establishes the agency's response framework for pandemic and infectious disease outbreaks including staff protection, patient triage, service modification protocols, and coordination with public health authorities for Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Pandemics and infectious disease outbreaks require rapid, coordinated, and sustained response to protect staff and patients while maintaining essential services.

2. Scope

This policy applies to all employees, contractors, per diem staff, and volunteers of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. It is activated by the Administrator upon declaration of a public health emergency by federal, state, or local authorities, or upon determination by the agency that an infectious disease outbreak poses a significant risk to staff or patients.

3. Definitions

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a Pandemic Response Plan that addresses preparation, response, and recovery phases.

4.2 The agency shall maintain a minimum 30-day supply of critical PPE at all times.

4.3 Staff protection shall be prioritized, including PPE provision, exposure protocols, and accommodation for high-risk staff.

4.4 Service delivery shall be modified as necessary during a pandemic to balance patient safety, staff safety, and essential service continuity.

4.5 The agency shall coordinate with local, state, and federal public health authorities during any outbreak or pandemic.

4.6 All pandemic response activities shall be documented and debriefed following event resolution.

POLICY CO-HP-101 — HIPAA, CMIA & Sensitive Data Privacy Management

Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes the comprehensive privacy management program for Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. governing the collection, use, disclosure, retention, and destruction of protected health information (PHI), electronic protected health information (ePHI), and sensitive categories of health data. This policy ensures simultaneous compliance with the HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR Part 160 and Part 164, Subparts A and E), the California Confidentiality of Medical Information Act (CMIA) (Cal. Civ. Code §§ 56–56.37), the Information Practices Act (Cal. Civ. Code § 1798 et seq.), and federal substance use disorder confidentiality requirements (42 CFR Part 2). This policy operationalizes all patient privacy rights, workforce privacy obligations, and sensitive data protections into a single, survey-defensible governance instrument.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

All members of the workforce of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. including employees, contractors, per diem staff, volunteers, students, and interns

All members of the Governing Body

The Agency Administrator

The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager

The Compliance Officer / Privacy Officer

All business associates and subcontractors who access, receive, create, maintain, or transmit PHI on behalf of the agency

All information systems, paper records, verbal communications, and electronic media containing PHI or ePHI

This policy does not apply to de-identified health information as defined under 45 CFR § 164.514(a)–(c), provided de-identification has been performed and documented per approved methodology.

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a comprehensive privacy program that satisfies all requirements of the HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart E), the CMIA (Cal. Civ. Code §§ 56–56.37), and 42 CFR Part 2 for substance use disorder records.

4.2 The agency shall designate a Privacy Officer with authority to develop, implement, and enforce all privacy policies and procedures. The Privacy Officer may be the same individual as the Compliance Officer, provided adequate authority and independence are maintained.

4.3 All uses and disclosures of PHI shall be limited to the minimum necessary to accomplish the intended purpose, per 45 CFR § 164.502(b) and policy CO-DG-101. Treatment, payment, and health care operations (TPO) uses are governed by role-based access profiles defining the minimum necessary for each job function.

4.4 The agency shall maintain and distribute a Notice of Privacy Practices (NPP) to all patients at the first service delivery contact, per 45 CFR § 164.520. The NPP shall describe all uses and disclosures, patient rights, and the agency's legal duties. A signed acknowledgment of receipt shall be obtained; if the patient declines to sign, the attempt and refusal shall be documented.

4.5 Patients have the following rights, which the agency shall honor within the timeframes required by HIPAA and California law:

Right to access PHI (45 CFR § 164.524) — responded to within 30 days (one 30-day extension permitted with written notice)

Right to request amendment of PHI (45 CFR § 164.526) — responded to within 60 days (one 30-day extension permitted)

Right to receive an accounting of disclosures (45 CFR § 164.528) — responded to within 60 days (one 30-day extension permitted)

Right to request restrictions on certain uses and disclosures (45 CFR § 164.522(a))

Right to request confidential communications (45 CFR § 164.522(b))

Right to receive a copy of the NPP (45 CFR § 164.520)

Right to file a complaint without retaliation

4.6 The agency shall apply heightened protections to the following categories of sensitive data, which are subject to more restrictive disclosure rules under California law and/or federal regulations:

Mental health records (Cal. Welf. & Inst. Code § 5328; CMIA)

HIV/AIDS test results and diagnosis (Cal. Health & Safety Code §§ 120975–121020)

Substance use disorder records (42 CFR Part 2)

Minor consent records (Cal. Fam. Code § 6920 et seq.)

Genetic information (GINA; Cal. Civ. Code § 56.17)

4.7 Substance use disorder records protected under 42 CFR Part 2 shall not be disclosed without the patient's specific written consent, except as permitted by 42 CFR Part 2 (medical emergency, qualified research, audit/evaluation, court order meeting § 2.64–2.67 requirements). Re-disclosure is prohibited and the agency shall include the Part 2 re-disclosure notice with any permitted disclosure.

4.8 All workforce members shall receive HIPAA privacy training within 14 calendar days of hire and annually thereafter. Training shall include CMIA requirements, sensitive data handling, and the agency's specific privacy procedures. Completion shall be documented and tracked per HR-TR-101.

4.9 Sanctions for privacy violations shall be applied consistently per CO-CP-004 (Code of Conduct & Ethics) and HR-ER-002 (Disciplinary Action & Progressive Discipline). Sanctions shall be proportionate to the severity of the violation and documented in the employee's personnel file. Failure to report a known privacy violation is itself a sanctionable offense.

4.10 Only the most current approved version of this policy shall be considered valid. Any revision requires re-acknowledgment by all workforce members within 14 calendar days of the revised effective date.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Privacy Program Governance

6.2 Notice of Privacy Practices (NPP)

6.3 Patient Rights Fulfillment

6.3.1 Right to Access

6.3.2 Right to Amendment

6.3.3 Right to Accounting of Disclosures

6.3.4 Right to Request Restrictions and Confidential Communications

6.4 Sensitive Data Protections

6.5 Workforce Privacy Training

6.6 Sanctions

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance Measurement

8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

8.2 Surveyor Expectations

CMS surveyors and state auditors will specifically verify:

NPP distribution and acknowledgment. Surveyors will review a sample of patient records to verify that the NPP was provided at the first service delivery contact and that an acknowledgment or documented refusal is present.

Patient rights fulfillment. Surveyors will review the Patient Rights Request Tracker and a sample of completed requests to verify timeliness and completeness of responses to access, amendment, and accounting requests.

Minimum necessary implementation. Surveyors will verify that the agency has implemented role-based access policies and that workforce members can articulate the minimum necessary principle.

Sensitive data protections. California Department of Public Health (CDPH) surveyors will verify CMIA compliance, HIV/AIDS confidentiality, and mental health record protections. Federal auditors may review 42 CFR Part 2 compliance for substance use disorder records.

Training and awareness. Surveyors will request training records and may interview staff regarding privacy procedures and patient rights.

Sanction policy and enforcement. Surveyors will verify that a sanction policy exists and has been applied when violations occurred.

8.3 Common Failure Points

9. References

9.1 Federal Regulations

9.2 California State Law

9.3 Cross-Referenced Agency Policies

10. Training Requirements

All workforce members shall receive comprehensive HIPAA/CMIA privacy training within 14 calendar days of hire/engagement. Training must cover all elements identified in Section 6.5.1. Training shall be delivered via the agency's LMS with documented completion.

Annual refresher privacy training shall be completed by all workforce members within 60 calendar days of the start of each calendar year. Content shall be updated annually by the Privacy Officer.

Targeted retraining shall be required for any workforce member involved in a privacy incident or audit finding, within 14 calendar days of incident closure.

All workforce members shall sign the Privacy & Confidentiality Acknowledgment Form at hire and annually thereafter, attesting to their understanding of HIPAA, CMIA, and sensitive data requirements.

The Privacy Officer shall maintain training records in the LMS and report completion rates in the quarterly compliance report.

11. Version Control

This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per EN-LC-001.

Only the most current approved version, as reflected in the policy header, is valid for any operational, compliance, or regulatory purpose. Superseded versions must be archived and clearly marked "SUPERSEDED — NOT FOR USE."

Any substantive revision requires: (a) review and approval by the Governing Body; (b) re-acknowledgment by all workforce members within 14 calendar days of the revised effective date; (c) update to the enterprise policy index per EN-TG-001.

Non-substantive revisions (formatting, typographical corrections, updated cross-references) may be approved by the Privacy Officer with notification to the Governing Body at the next regular meeting. Non-substantive revisions do not require re-acknowledgment.

POLICY CO-BA-101 — Business Associate & Vendor PHI Management

Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes the requirements for identifying, qualifying, contracting with, monitoring, and terminating business associates and vendors who access, create, receive, maintain, or transmit protected health information (PHI) on behalf of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. This policy ensures compliance with the HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR § 164.502(e) and § 164.504(e)), the HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR § 164.314), the HITECH Act (42 U.S.C. § 17931 et seq.), and the California Confidentiality of Medical Information Act (CMIA) (Cal. Civ. Code § 56.10(c)). The agency shall not permit any entity to access PHI without an executed Business Associate Agreement (BAA) that meets all regulatory requirements.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

All third-party entities that access, create, receive, maintain, or transmit PHI on behalf of the agency, including but not limited to: electronic health record (EHR) vendors, billing/coding services, cloud storage providers, IT service providers, shredding services, interpreters/translation services, collection agencies, consultants, auditors, and legal counsel

All workforce members who engage, manage, or oversee vendor relationships involving PHI

The Compliance Officer / Privacy Officer

The Administrator

The IT Director / CISO

All subcontractor relationships through which PHI may flow downstream

This policy does not apply to: (a) disclosures to treating providers for treatment purposes (45 CFR § 164.502(a)(1)(ii)); (b) disclosures to plan sponsors per 45 CFR § 164.504(f); (c) conduit exceptions (postal services, internet service providers acting solely as conduits).

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall execute a compliant BAA with every business associate prior to permitting access to PHI, per 45 CFR § 164.502(e)(1) and CMIA Cal. Civ. Code § 56.10(c). No PHI shall be shared, transmitted, or made accessible to any entity until a fully executed BAA is on file.

4.2 The agency shall maintain a Business Associate Master Registry documenting all active and terminated business associate relationships, including: entity name, services provided, PHI categories accessed, BAA execution date, BAA expiration/renewal date, risk classification, and assigned internal owner.

4.3 All vendors with potential PHI access shall be classified into a risk tier prior to BAA execution:

Tier 1 — High Risk: Entities with direct, ongoing, and unrestricted access to PHI (e.g., EHR vendors, billing services, cloud hosting providers)

Tier 2 — Moderate Risk: Entities with limited or role-restricted access to PHI (e.g., consultants, auditors)

Tier 3 — Low Risk: Entities with incidental or one-time access potential (e.g., shredding services, on-site equipment maintenance)

4.4 BAA content shall include, at minimum, all elements required by 45 CFR § 164.504(e)(2) and § 164.314(a)(2), including but not limited to: (a) permitted uses and disclosures; (b) obligation to safeguard PHI; (c) obligation to report breaches; (d) obligation to make PHI available for patient access requests; (e) obligation to return or destroy PHI upon termination; (f) subcontractor requirements; (g) termination provisions.

4.5 The agency shall conduct vendor due diligence prior to BAA execution including: (a) verification of entity's HIPAA compliance program; (b) review of security controls for Tier 1 and Tier 2 vendors; (c) OIG/SAM exclusion screening; (d) reference verification for new Tier 1 vendors.

4.6 Business associate relationships shall be monitored throughout the term. Tier 1 vendors shall be reviewed annually, including confirmation that the vendor has not been excluded from federal programs and that no material changes have occurred in the vendor's security posture or services.

4.7 Upon termination of a business associate relationship, the agency shall ensure: (a) return or destruction of all PHI held by the business associate; (b) written certification of PHI destruction or return; (c) revocation of all system access within 24 hours of termination; (d) update of the Business Associate Master Registry.

4.8 Business associates are directly liable for breach notification to the agency within the timeframes specified in the BAA (not to exceed 30 calendar days of discovery, per HITECH). The agency shall include breach responsibility provisions in all BAAs.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Identification and Risk Classification

6.2 Due Diligence and BAA Execution

6.3 Ongoing Monitoring

6.4 Termination and Offboarding

6.5 Breach Responsibility

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance Measurement

8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

8.2 Surveyor Expectations

Surveyors will request the Business Associate Master Registry and select a sample of BAAs for review.

Surveyors will verify that BAAs contain all required elements per 45 CFR § 164.504(e).

Surveyors will ask whether the agency has a process for monitoring business associate compliance and what happens when a BA reports a breach.

CDPH surveyors may verify CMIA authorization requirements for vendor PHI access.

8.3 Common Failure Points

9. References

9.1 Federal Regulations

9.2 California State Law

9.3 Cross-Referenced Agency Policies

10. Training Requirements

All workforce members who manage or oversee vendor relationships shall receive training on this policy within 14 calendar days of assuming vendor management responsibilities.

The Compliance Officer shall include business associate management in annual compliance training, covering: (a) identifying business associates; (b) the "no BAA, no access" requirement; (c) monitoring responsibilities; (d) breach reporting obligations.

All Department Heads shall be trained on vendor identification requirements and their obligation to report new vendor relationships to the Compliance Officer.

11. Version Control

This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per EN-LC-001.

Only the most current approved version is valid. Superseded versions must be archived and marked "SUPERSEDED — NOT FOR USE."

Substantive revision requires Governing Body approval, re-acknowledgment within 14 calendar days, and enterprise policy index update per EN-TG-001.

Non-substantive revisions may be approved by the Compliance Officer with notification to the Governing Body.

POLICY CO-IR-101 — Security Incident Response & Breach Notification

Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes the comprehensive incident response and breach notification program for Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. covering the detection, classification, investigation, containment, remediation, breach determination, notification, and documentation of security incidents and breaches involving protected health information (PHI) and personally identifiable information (PII). This policy ensures compliance with the HIPAA Breach Notification Rule (45 CFR §§ 164.400–164.414), the HITECH Act (42 U.S.C. § 17932), California data breach notification law (Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.82), and the CMIA breach provisions (Cal. Civ. Code § 56.36).

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

All incidents involving the unauthorized acquisition, access, use, or disclosure of PHI, ePHI, or PII maintained by Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc.

All workforce members, business associates, subcontractors, and any entity with access to agency PHI

All information media — electronic, paper, verbal, and visual

All locations where PHI is stored, processed, transmitted, or accessed

4. Policy Statements

4.1 All workforce members shall report suspected or confirmed security incidents to the Privacy Officer and IT Director within 1 hour of discovery. Failure to report a suspected incident is a sanctionable offense.

4.2 The agency shall classify all security incidents using a standardized severity framework:

Level 1 — Critical: Confirmed breach affecting ≥ 500 individuals; ransomware affecting PHI systems; confirmed unauthorized access to sensitive data categories

Level 2 — High: Confirmed breach affecting < 500 individuals; unauthorized disclosure of PHI to a single unauthorized recipient; lost or stolen device containing unencrypted PHI

Level 3 — Moderate: Unauthorized access to PHI without evidence of acquisition or viewing; misdirected fax or email to wrong recipient (PHI not accessed)

Level 4 — Low: Near-miss events; policy violations without PHI exposure; unsuccessful phishing attempts

4.3 For every incident involving PHI, the Privacy Officer shall conduct the HIPAA 4-factor risk assessment per 45 CFR § 164.402(2) to determine whether a breach has occurred:

Factor 1: Nature and extent of PHI involved (types of identifiers, likelihood of re-identification)

Factor 2: Unauthorized person who used the PHI or to whom the disclosure was made

Factor 3: Whether the PHI was actually acquired or viewed

Factor 4: Extent to which risk to the PHI has been mitigated

4.4 If the 4-factor risk assessment demonstrates greater than a low probability that PHI has been compromised, the incident is a reportable breach under HIPAA. All three exceptions must also be evaluated: (a) unintentional acquisition by workforce member acting under authority (45 CFR § 164.402(1)(i)); (b) inadvertent disclosure between authorized persons (45 CFR § 164.402(1)(ii)); (c) good faith belief that unauthorized person could not retain information (45 CFR § 164.402(1)(iii)).

4.5 Notification timelines:

Individual notification (HIPAA): Without unreasonable delay, not later than 60 calendar days from the date of discovery of the breach (45 CFR § 164.404(b))

HHS notification (≥ 500 individuals): Within 60 calendar days via HHS breach portal (45 CFR § 164.408(b))

HHS notification (< 500 individuals): Within 60 calendar days after the end of the calendar year in which the breach was discovered (45 CFR § 164.408(c))

Media notification (≥ 500 individuals in a single state/jurisdiction): Within 60 calendar days (45 CFR § 164.406)

California notification (Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.82): In the most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay. If breach involves ≥ 500 California residents, notify the California Attorney General

CMIA notification: If breach of medical information, notify per Cal. Civ. Code § 56.36

4.6 All investigations shall be completed within 30 calendar days of incident discovery. The Privacy Officer and IT Director shall co-lead investigations involving ePHI. The Compliance Officer shall be notified of all Level 1 and Level 2 incidents within 2 hours.

4.7 The agency shall conduct a post-incident review for all Level 1 and Level 2 incidents, including root cause analysis per QA-AE-002 and corrective action development per QA-AE-003.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Incident Detection and Reporting

6.2 Investigation

6.3 Breach Determination and Notification

6.4 Remediation and Post-Incident Review

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance Measurement

8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

8.2 Surveyor Expectations

Surveyors will review the Security Incident Tracker for evidence of a functioning incident response program.

Surveyors will request 4-factor risk assessment documentation for any incidents during the survey look-back period.

Surveyors will verify notification timeliness and content compliance.

CDPH surveyors may specifically ask about California breach notification compliance.

8.3 Common Failure Points

9. References

9.1 Federal Regulations

9.2 California State Law

9.3 Cross-Referenced Agency Policies

10. Training Requirements

All workforce members shall receive incident reporting training within 14 calendar days of hire, covering: incident recognition, reporting procedures, and reporting timelines. Refreshed annually.

The Incident Response Team shall receive annual tabletop exercise training on breach response scenarios, including 4-factor risk assessment, notification procedures, and California-specific requirements.

The Privacy Officer shall complete annual breach notification regulatory update training.

11. Version Control

Per enterprise standard (EN-LC-001). Only current version is valid. Substantive revision requires Governing Body approval and re-acknowledgment within 14 calendar days.

POLICY CO-DG-101 — Data Governance & Minimum Necessary Enforcement

Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes the data governance program for Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. governing the lifecycle of protected health information (PHI) and electronic protected health information (ePHI) from creation through destruction. This policy operationalizes the HIPAA minimum necessary standard (45 CFR § 164.502(b)), defines access control validation requirements, mandates data minimization practices, enforces export and download controls, prevents unauthorized shadow systems, and ensures alignment with record retention requirements. This policy serves as the enterprise-level governance instrument for PHI lifecycle management and data stewardship.

3. Scope

This policy applies to all PHI and ePHI created, received, maintained, or transmitted by the agency in any medium, and to all workforce members, business associates, and systems that access, process, or store such data.

4. Policy Statements

4.1 The agency shall implement a PHI lifecycle management framework governing data creation, collection, use, disclosure, storage, transmission, archival, and destruction. Each phase shall have defined controls, responsible parties, and audit mechanisms.

4.2 The minimum necessary standard (45 CFR § 164.502(b)) shall be operationalized through role-based access profiles. Each job function shall have a defined PHI access profile specifying: (a) which categories of PHI the role may access; (b) the volume of records accessible; (c) the permitted uses; (d) the permitted disclosure recipients. Access profiles shall be reviewed annually.

4.3 Data minimization shall be enforced at every point of PHI handling: (a) collect only the PHI required for the identified purpose; (b) use only the PHI required to perform the task; (c) disclose only the PHI required by the recipient; (d) retain only the PHI required by the retention schedule.

4.4 All PHI exports, downloads, bulk queries, and external transmissions shall require documented justification and shall be logged. Bulk exports (≥ 50 records) shall require supervisory approval prior to execution.

4.5 Shadow systems — any unauthorized repository of PHI outside agency-approved systems (including personal drives, personal email, USB storage, personal cloud accounts, spreadsheets, and non-approved applications) — are prohibited. Violation constitutes a sanctionable offense.

4.6 PHI retention and destruction shall comply with CO-HP-007 (Record Retention & Destruction). Data subject to litigation hold shall be preserved per RM-ER-006 regardless of retention schedule.

4.7 The IT Director / CISO shall implement technical controls supporting data governance including: (a) role-based access control in the EHR and all PHI systems; (b) automatic session timeouts; (c) export/download logging; (d) DLP (Data Loss Prevention) monitoring where technically feasible; (e) encryption per IT-SC-003.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 PHI Lifecycle Governance

6.2 Minimum Necessary Access Control

6.3 Export, Download, and Transmission Controls

6.4 Shadow System Prevention

6.5 Retention Alignment

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance Measurement

POLICY CO-FW-101 — Fraud, Waste & Abuse Prevention

Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes the comprehensive fraud, waste, and abuse (FWA) prevention, detection, investigation, and remediation program for Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. This policy ensures compliance with the federal False Claims Act (31 U.S.C. §§ 3729–3733), the Anti-Kickback Statute (42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7b(b)), the Stark Law (42 U.S.C. § 1395nn), the Deficit Reduction Act of 2005 (§ 6032), OIG Compliance Program Guidance for Home Health Agencies, and CMS program integrity requirements.

3. Scope

This policy applies to all workforce members, Governing Body members, contractors, subcontractors, agents, and business associates of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. in connection with all federal and state healthcare program participation.

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. maintains a zero-tolerance policy for fraud, waste, and abuse. All workforce members are responsible for preventing, detecting, and reporting suspected FWA.

4.2 The agency shall maintain the following definitions:

Fraud: Knowingly and willfully executing or attempting to execute a scheme to defraud any healthcare program or to obtain money or property by means of false pretenses, representations, or promises.

Waste: Overutilization of services or practices that directly or indirectly result in unnecessary costs to federal healthcare programs, whether due to mismanagement, deficient practices, or abusive practices.

Abuse: Actions inconsistent with sound fiscal, business, or medical practices that result in unnecessary cost or in reimbursement for services not medically necessary or that fail to meet professionally recognized standards.

4.3 The agency shall provide accessible reporting mechanisms for suspected FWA including: (a) the compliance hotline per CO-CP-006; (b) direct report to the Compliance Officer; (c) written report via the compliance mailbox; (d) anonymous reporting option. Reports may be made anonymously and shall be protected under the agency's non-retaliation policy (CO-CP-005).

4.4 No workforce member shall be retaliated against for reporting suspected FWA in good faith. Retaliation is itself a sanctionable offense subject to immediate disciplinary action up to and including termination and referral to legal counsel.

4.5 All reported or detected FWA concerns shall be investigated per CO-CP-007 (Compliance Investigation Process). The Compliance Officer shall lead or oversee all investigations with appropriate independence.

4.6 Upon confirmation of FWA, the agency shall: (a) cease the fraudulent, wasteful, or abusive practice immediately; (b) quantify overpayment if applicable; (c) refund overpayments within 60 calendar days of identification per 42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7k(d) and the CMS 60-day repayment rule; (d) report to appropriate federal/state authorities as required by law; (e) implement corrective action per QA-AE-003; (f) apply workforce sanctions per HR-ER-002.

4.7 Disciplinary actions for confirmed FWA involvement include but are not limited to: (a) mandatory retraining; (b) written reprimand; (c) suspension; (d) termination; (e) referral to law enforcement; (f) referral to professional licensing boards.

4.8 The agency shall conduct proactive FWA monitoring including: (a) billing pattern analysis per FN-FP-007; (b) claims audit sampling per CO-RA-002; (c) visit documentation vs. claims reconciliation per CO-DC-004; (d) referral pattern monitoring per CO-FA-001.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.2 Detection and Reporting

6.3 Investigation and Response

6.4 Corrective Action and Sanctions

POLICY CO-AI-101 — AI & Automated Systems Governance

Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes governance requirements for the use of artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), large language models (LLMs), and automated systems in the operations of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. This policy ensures that AI-assisted tools are used responsibly, transparently, and in compliance with HIPAA, the CMIA, CMS Conditions of Participation, and applicable professional standards. No AI or automated system shall make autonomous clinical decisions, generate fabricated documentation, or process PHI without authorization and safeguards.

3. Scope

This policy applies to all AI, ML, LLM, robotic process automation (RPA), and other automated systems used by the agency for any purpose including but not limited to: clinical decision support, documentation assistance, coding/billing support, scheduling optimization, quality analysis, predictive analytics, and administrative automation. This policy applies to all workforce members, contractors, and vendors who develop, deploy, or use such systems in connection with agency operations.

4. Policy Statements

4.1 No AI or automated system shall make autonomous clinical decisions. All clinical decisions — including diagnosis, treatment planning, medication management, care plan modifications, and patient assessments — require human clinical judgment by a licensed professional. AI may provide decision support inputs, but the licensed clinician retains full accountability for the clinical decision.

4.2 All AI-generated content used in clinical documentation, OASIS assessments, or care planning must be reviewed, validated, and authenticated by the responsible licensed clinician before becoming part of the clinical record. The clinician's signature on an AI-assisted document constitutes attestation that the content is accurate and reflects the clinician's independent professional judgment.

4.3 No AI system shall fabricate, hallucinate, or generate clinical observations, patient assessments, vital signs, interview responses, or any other clinical data. All clinical documentation must reflect actual patient encounters and direct clinical observations. Use of AI to generate fictitious clinical content constitutes fraud and is subject to immediate termination and potential legal referral.

4.4 PHI shall not be entered into, processed by, or transmitted to any AI system unless: (a) the system has been approved by the agency's IT Director / CISO and Compliance Officer; (b) a BAA is in place if the system is operated by a third party; (c) the system meets HIPAA Security Rule technical safeguard requirements; (d) data minimization principles are applied (only the minimum necessary PHI is used).

4.5 All AI systems used in agency operations shall be classified and approved:

Category A — Approved for PHI: Systems that have undergone full security assessment, BAA execution (if external), and privacy impact analysis. Listed on the Approved AI Systems Registry.

Category B — Approved, No PHI: Systems approved for use with de-identified data or non-PHI operational data only.

Category C — Prohibited: Systems that have not been assessed or that have failed assessment. Use of Category C systems with agency data is a sanctionable offense.

4.6 All AI system outputs affecting patient care, coding, billing, or compliance decisions shall be auditable. The agency shall maintain the ability to trace any AI-assisted decision or output to: (a) the input data; (b) the AI system used; (c) the human who reviewed and approved the output; (d) the date/time of review.

4.7 The agency shall maintain an AI Use Register documenting all AI systems in use, their category, purpose, data inputs, PHI exposure, approval status, responsible department, and review date.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 AI System Approval

6.2 AI Use in Clinical Documentation

6.3 Prohibited Uses

6.4 Monitoring and Audit

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance Measurement

10–11. Training Requirements & Version Control

All workforce members using AI tools shall receive training on this policy within 14 days of hire or first AI tool use. Training must cover: approved vs. prohibited uses, human validation requirement, fabrication prohibition, PHI restrictions, and reporting obligations. Annual refresher required. Version control per EN-LC-001.

POLICY RM-OS-101 — Cal/OSHA Occupational Safety Program (IIPP)

Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes the comprehensive Cal/OSHA occupational safety and health program for Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. as required by the California Injury and Illness Prevention Program (IIPP) standard (Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 3203). This policy integrates all Cal/OSHA requirements applicable to a home health agency operating in California, including but not limited to: IIPP core elements, Workplace Violence Prevention (SB 553; Cal. Lab. Code § 6401.9), Bloodborne Pathogens Exposure Control (8 CCR § 5193), Aerosol Transmissible Diseases (8 CCR § 5199), Personal Protective Equipment (8 CCR § 3380 et seq.), Hazard Communication (8 CCR § 5194), ergonomic safety for patient handling, heat illness prevention (8 CCR § 3395), and field/driving safety for home health workers.

3. Scope

This policy applies to all employees, contractors, per diem staff, students, interns, and volunteers of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. who perform work activities in any location including the agency's office, patient homes, community settings, and while traveling for agency business.

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain an Injury and Illness Prevention Program (IIPP) as the foundation of its occupational safety program, per Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 3203. The IIPP includes all seven required elements: (a) responsibility; (b) compliance; (c) communication; (d) hazard assessment; (e) accident/exposure investigation; (f) hazard correction; (g) training and instruction.

4.2 The agency designates the Risk Manager (or Administrator if no dedicated Risk Manager exists) as the person with authority and responsibility for implementing and maintaining the IIPP, per § 3203(a)(1).

4.3 Workplace Violence Prevention. The agency shall maintain a Workplace Violence Prevention Plan (WVPP) per Cal. Lab. Code § 6401.9 (SB 553), effective July 1, 2024. The WVPP shall: (a) identify the plan administrator; (b) include procedures for employee involvement in plan development; (c) define methods for accepting and responding to workplace violence reports; (d) establish communication procedures; (e) include emergency response protocols; (f) document workplace violence hazard assessments; (g) establish post-incident response and investigation procedures; (h) include training requirements. The WVPP shall be maintained as a written document accessible to all employees and Cal/OSHA.

4.4 Bloodborne Pathogens. The agency shall maintain an Exposure Control Plan (ECP) per 8 CCR § 5193, updated at least annually, identifying all job classifications with occupational exposure to blood and other potentially infectious materials (OPIM), the exposure determination, the schedule and method of implementing standard precautions, engineering controls, work practice controls, hepatitis B vaccination program, post-exposure evaluation and follow-up, training, and recordkeeping.

4.5 Aerosol Transmissible Diseases (ATD). The agency shall maintain an ATD Exposure Control Plan per 8 CCR § 5199, applicable to all employees who provide services in settings where occupational exposure to aerosol transmissible diseases may occur. The plan shall include: source identification, referral and transfer procedures, respiratory protection (N95 or higher), medical surveillance, training, exposure incident management, and surge capacity.

4.6 PPE. The agency shall provide, at no cost to employees, all personal protective equipment required for their job duties per 8 CCR § 3380 et seq. PPE selection shall be based on job hazard analysis. Training on proper use, maintenance, and limitations shall be provided at hire and when new hazards or PPE are introduced.

4.7 Hazard Communication. The agency shall maintain a Hazard Communication Program per 8 CCR § 5194, including: (a) written program; (b) Safety Data Sheets (SDS) for all hazardous chemicals present; (c) container labeling per GHS; (d) employee training on chemical hazards, SDS interpretation, and protective measures.

4.8 Incident Reporting and Investigation. All work-related injuries, illnesses, exposures, and near-misses shall be reported to the Risk Manager within 24 hours. The Risk Manager shall investigate all incidents to determine root cause and implement corrective actions per QA-AE-002 and QA-AE-003.

4.9 Ergonomics / Patient Handling. Clinical staff performing patient handling (lifting, transferring, repositioning) shall be trained in safe patient handling techniques and the use of available assistive equipment. The agency shall evaluate ergonomic hazards in patient care activities and implement controls.

4.10 Heat Illness Prevention. For employees who work outdoors or in environments without adequate climate control (including traveling between patient homes in extreme heat), the agency shall implement heat illness prevention measures per 8 CCR § 3395, including: (a) provision of water; (b) access to shade/cool-down areas; (c) high heat procedures; (d) emergency response.

4.11 Driving / Field Safety. All employees who drive for agency business shall comply with motor vehicle safety requirements per RM-SS-003. Additional field safety measures include: (a) pre-visit safety assessment; (b) check-in/check-out procedures; (c) high-risk visit protocols per RM-SS-001; (d) prohibition on distracted driving.

POLICY HR-TR-101 — Workforce Training, Competency & Policy Acknowledgment

Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes the comprehensive workforce training, competency validation, and policy acknowledgment program for Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. This policy ensures all workforce members receive required training across all regulatory domains (HIPAA, OSHA, infection control, fraud/waste/abuse, CMS CoP, California-specific requirements), that competency is validated through defined assessment methods, that all training is tracked in the Learning Management System (LMS), and that policy acknowledgments are documented and monitored. This policy satisfies training and competency requirements under 42 CFR Part 484, HIPAA (45 CFR § 164.530(b)), Cal/OSHA (8 CCR § 3203), and OIG Compliance Program Guidance.

3. Scope

This policy applies to all employees, contractors, per diem staff, volunteers, students, and interns of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. All workforce members must complete required training regardless of employment status.

4. Policy Statements

4.1 All workforce members shall complete mandatory training per the agency's Training Requirements Matrix within the timeframes defined for each topic. The Training Requirements Matrix shall be maintained by the HR Director in consultation with the Compliance Officer, Director of Nursing, Risk Manager, and IT Director.

4.3 Clinical staff shall additionally complete discipline-specific competency evaluation per HR-TD-003 and CL-SD-008.

Failed assessments require retraining and reassessment within 14 calendar days.

4.6 All workforce members shall sign a Policy Acknowledgment Form per GV-PM-003 for all policies applicable to their role: (a) within 14 calendar days of hire; (b) within 14 calendar days of any policy revision; (c) annually upon each policy's review date if re-acknowledgment is required by the policy.

4.7 Workforce members who fail to complete required training within the specified timeframe shall be subject to: (a) first occurrence — written notice with 7-day extension; (b) second occurrence — mandatory meeting with supervisor and HR; (c) third occurrence — suspension from patient care (clinical staff) or non-patient-care duties pending completion; (d) continued non-compliance — disciplinary action per HR-ER-002.

POLICY HR-EH-101 — Employee Health, Exposure & Occupational Clearance

Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes the employee health, occupational exposure management, and fitness-for-duty program for Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. This policy ensures compliance with California TB screening requirements (Cal. Health & Safety Code § 121525; Cal. Code Regs., tit. 17, § 2593), Cal/OSHA bloodborne pathogen exposure requirements (8 CCR § 5193), Cal/OSHA aerosol transmissible disease requirements (8 CCR § 5199), hepatitis B vaccination mandates, occupational exposure incident management, fitness-for-duty evaluation, and return-to-work clearance. This policy protects both the workforce and the patients served by ensuring that employees are medically screened, vaccinated as required, and fit to perform their duties safely.

3. Scope

This policy applies to all employees, contractors, per diem staff, students, interns, and volunteers who perform direct patient care or have occupational exposure to blood, OPIM, or aerosol transmissible pathogens.

4. Policy Statements

4.1 TB Screening. All employees shall undergo tuberculosis risk assessment and screening per California law (Cal. Health & Safety Code § 121525; 17 CCR § 2593):

Pre-employment: TB risk assessment and, if indicated, TB test (TST or IGRA) prior to patient contact. Employees with a positive TB test shall have a chest X-ray and medical evaluation to rule out active disease.

Annual: Annual TB risk assessment. Repeat TB testing as indicated by risk assessment or upon known exposure.

Post-exposure: TB testing within 8–10 weeks of a significant exposure to a person with suspected or confirmed active TB.

4.2 Vaccination Tracking. The agency shall maintain vaccination records for all employees with occupational exposure:

Hepatitis B: Offered within 10 working days of initial assignment per 8 CCR § 5193. Three-dose series tracked; declination documented.

Influenza: Annual vaccination recommended; declination documented.

COVID-19: Per current CDPH and CMS requirements.

Other: As required by public health order or facility-specific requirements.

4.3 Exposure Response. For all occupational exposure incidents (bloodborne, airborne, or other hazardous material):

Immediate first aid and decontamination

Medical evaluation within 24 hours (BBP) or as clinically indicated (ATD/chemical)

Source patient testing (with consent) if applicable

Employee testing per post-exposure protocol

Follow-up testing at intervals defined by the agency's Exposure Control Plan and medical provider

Workers' compensation claim initiation per HR-WM-004

4.4 Fit-for-Duty. Employees must be medically fit to perform the essential functions of their position. Fit-for-duty evaluation may be required: (a) prior to initial assignment; (b) upon return from medical leave exceeding 5 consecutive calendar days; (c) when a supervisor has documented concerns about an employee's ability to perform essential functions safely; (d) per Cal/OSHA medical surveillance requirements (e.g., respirator use medical clearance per 8 CCR § 5144).

4.5 Return-to-Work Clearance. Employees returning to duty after: (a) work-related injury or illness; (b) medical leave exceeding 5 calendar days; (c) occupational exposure requiring treatment; or (d) communicable disease must provide written medical clearance from a licensed healthcare provider specifying: (i) fitness to return to full or modified duty; (ii) any work restrictions; (iii) duration of restrictions (if any). Modified duty accommodations shall be evaluated per ADA and FEHA requirements.
